city-digital-twin · Newcastle study · project report

A second city requires verified physics and sampling

2026-09-18HEAD e37035dbranch praneetdhoolia/mumbai-digital-twingate PASS quick / FAIL full package

The existing simulator is not yet an accurate all-mode twin. A reproduced sampling defect leaves standing capacity at full size in the latest completed 25% run. Mumbai needs its own observations, mode and operator contracts, and measured scaling validation. This report preserves verified evidence and identifies unfinished review scopes explicitly.

Method

Three delegated reviewers stopped on workspace credit errors. Coordinator preserved available evidence and continued locally. Unreviewed scopes remain explicit gaps. All three collectors completed. The twelve-mode table was regenerated from the latest fit and target artefacts. No run launched, no holdout opened, no handoff performed.

ferry0.05555274986111813 vs 0.1429 → -61.1 %0.05555274986111813 → -61.1 %derived: DERIVED, not observed: no Newcastle ferry patronage is published in any acquired artefact - the Opal all-modes Ferry series is NSW-wide and Sydney-dominated, and the station entries/exits publication carries Train and Light rail only. The one city-specific ferry observation that exists is the census G62 one-method count, 34 of 904 PT journeys (3.761%), and it sets the ferry share WITHIN public transport, which the HTS PT level then scales. Two things make that transfer more defensible for this mode than for the others: the Stockton service is a CAPTIVE crossing (the road alternative is a ~20 km detour via Hexham), so its riders are not choosing it on the margin the way a bus rider might; and a share WITHIN PT is far less sensitive to the August 2021 lockdown than an absolute level, because the lockdown suppressed the numerator and denominator together. The coal chain has run on dedicated grade-separated track since 2006 (ARTC/PWCS/NCIG, ~110 movements/day), so the only real road interaction is the level crossings - and those are DERIVED, not assumed: one closure per scheduled passenger train that crosses, at the time it crosses (9.90; Clyde Street 203, Saint James Road 110, 313/weekday, each 160 s), plus the freight movements the 2012 Cobbora Coal environmental assessment survey counted at these two crossings (9.167, #184; Clyde Street 48, Saint James Road 44, each 277 s, spread over the day because no freight timetable is published). 405 closures/weekday in total.     Builds the network layer the scenarios will run on. Nothing here is a result — no scenario has been executed. The MATSim network, the 15 mapped schedules and the SUMO corridor nets are inputs. ## The finding that reshaped task 1 DECISIONS.md §3.1 quoted the network-wide imputation rate (75.4% of lane counts) and concluded that manual aerial correction of Hunter/Scott was required before any B3 net-arrivals figure. Measured on the corridor — the 40 Hunter/Scott edges within 60 m of the alignment, 4.08 km — the rates invert: | Field | Corridor trunk observed | Network-wide imputed | |---|---:|---:| | num_lanes | 87.5% | 75.4% | | speed_limit_kmh | 97.5% | 53.7% | | kerbside_use | 27.5% | 98.0% | The as-built cross-section reads lanes=1, oneway=yes, maxspeed=40, matching NSW Movement and Place ("one lane of traffic in each direction on Hunter and Scott streets between Worth Place and Telford Street"). The corridor cross streets, at 23.8%, are what §3.1's average was really measuring. So the hand correction isn't needed for the as-built network. What cannot be observed is the corridor *without* the tram, and that is now an explicit assumption swep

    ## What this is The first thing P4 does is execute MATSim. I pointed it at scenarios/matsim/S2/WEEKDAY/ — the artefact P3 delivered — and it refused to load. So did the other 29. P3 verified those 30 sets thoroughly *as data*, and every one of those statements is still true: the day-type split partitions the mapped schedule exactly, all 1,714 route link sequences are byte-identical to source, the stop→link map is unchanged, no stop dangles, the E1 patch reproduces the base build's counts. The checks were asking whether the artefacts were internally consistent. They were never asking whether a simulator could read them. ## Three defects | # | Defect | Reach | Symptom | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | The day-type filter round-trips the schedule through ElementTree, which drops the doctype | all 30 | MATSim selects its reader *from* the doctype; parse fails at line 2 with a null-delegate SAXParseException | | 2 | Removing two thirds of the routes orphans the stop facilities and minimalTransferTimes relations only they served — 113 + 42 on S2/WEEKDAY, 2,193 + 1,034 on S0/SAT | all 30 | SwissRailRaptorData.calculateRouteStopTransfers dereferences a null array.     • The mode-choice specification work, ending with the issue-32 rebuild batch (STATUS task 4.1) executed end to end on 16 August. The simulator now runs on a package where every declared value reaches the model, the demand carries its five specification fixes, and the full gate suite is green.
    • Every open issue was re-measured against today's model before anything was touched — [cities/newcastle/docs/audit/ISSUE_VERDICTS.md](cities/newcastle/docs/audit/ISSUE_VERDICTS.md) is the record (3 FALSE parts, 2 CHANGED, 7 CONFIRMED, 2 UNTESTABLE), and its 16 August addendum records what the rebuild then resolved. The board ([STATUS.md](cities/newcastle/docs/STATUS.md)) now carries one numbered plan with ETAs in place of the old scattered task lists.
    • - Harvest (#32): 10/10 OSM layers over the boundary-derived extent, every layer larger than its osm_pre_issue32 counterpart. Core SA1s without a road node: 99 → 4, with 0 agents in them — all 35,365 stranded agents are on the network.
    • - Network: 181,892 links carrying the declared speeds; all 15 GTFS feeds mapped in one pt2matsim build, 0 unmapped stops each; scenario feeds rebuilt from declarations first.
    • - Demand, regenerated once with five fixes (DECISIONS.md §9.38–§9.41):
    • - destination decay solved per purpose × home LGA — all 30 cells land on their own HTS distance row (Newcastle education 3.0 km, was 6.57; Port Stephens shopping was unreachable until this harvest restored its attractors — direct confirmation of the #32 contamination);
    • - zero 30-hour-day collisions on all three day types (#37 acceptance met);
    • - through-traffic tier live at 3 gates (M1 48,016 · Hunter Expressway 33,882 · Pacific Highway 20,701), car-locked, seeded from calibration counts only (#20);
    • - bike availability drawn at a declared, swept 0.50 instead of silently universal (#29 mechanism);
    • - business travel deliberately NOT rebuilt (already generated at 2.11% vs 2.0% observed).
    • - One more stale-extent defect fixed in flight: the DEM tile list was typed in for the old extent; it is now derived from the boundary + harvest margin, and gradient coverage is 100% on roads and footways.
    • check_package 1,452 checks ALL PASSED (2 standing warnings, both owned) · check_hardcoding --strict 0 items, reach 69/69 · manifest 391 files · smoke run smoke_postrebuild rc=0 with a conforming _run.json (median iteration 10.1 s at 1%, vs 9.8 s on the smaller network). Nothing in this repository is a result.
    • - Zero-hardcoding: the config is emitted from 297 declared registry fields (no template, no patching); a second city runs the framework unchanged (13/13).
    • - A bare python run.py now starts the default 25% × 1,000-iteration run from a committed overlay (default_25pct) that names its provenance; --run-config smoke keeps the plumbing test.
    • Freight (#24) is the next focused change (truck mode + vehicle types). The #5 convergence pilot and everything downstream (ASC re-solve #9, calibrated base #14, #28's residual, #29's sizing) are run campaigns on these artefacts, not diff content.     ## What this does Builds Tier 1 of the ride pairing — a car passenger names the household member who drives them — and, in measuring it, finds that **the demand almost never contains a driver to name**. The second half is the more important half. Closes nothing. Issue #31 moves from *"unmodelled"* to *"modelled, and measured to be starved of supply"*. --- ## 1. The mechanism RidePairingEngine is a BeforeMobsim listener. MATSim's loop is replan → all plans final → mobsim, so at that boundary every selected plan is stable — that is the timetable, and a passenger only ever needs to *look up* a driver rather than search for one. This is what replaced the socnetsim joint-plans attempt that was measured at ~10× and reverted: a pairing baked into *plans* is destroyed by SubtourModeChoice; a pairing made *after* replanning is not. A paired passenger takes the driver's realised (previous-iteration) travel time — which is where the sample-dependent queueing lives that a teleported passenger is structurally immune to. An unpaired leg behaves exactly as before. The one design decision worth reviewing. decideOnLegTravelTime is `route.getTravelTime().or(leg.getTravel

    • ## 1. Which mode next — ranked separately, not lumped
    • Five of nine are already physical, measured rather than assumed: 1,448 buses sharing 22,102 road links with cars, 332 trains, 252 trams (21 links on-street), 107 ferries — 2,139 transit vehicles moving every iteration. The gap is passengers, motorbikes, taxis and Uber, not the fleet.
    • | 1 | Car passengers | 32.7% | mechanism BUILT, starved — one demand defect away |
    • | 2 | Freight | 6.52% MEASURED | cheap, measured, changes congestion for *every* mode |
    • | 3 | Taxis + Uber | 0.4–1.5% | DEFER — a 1% refinement must not precede a 33% defect |
    • | 4 | Motorbikes | unknown | STAY DECLINED — HTS gives no trip-share target at all |
    • Freight outranks taxis deliberately: it is *measured* rather than inferred, it is 6.5× the share, and a heavy vehicle at PCE > 1 changes the travel time of every car, bus and tram on its links — it improves the denominator every mode is judged against.
    • ## 2. What data we have on how people choose a mode
    • The behavioural layer is 55 fields: 20 assumed, 12 literature, 11 measured, 8 derived, 4 definition — so 58% of how this model decides a mode is not measured here. That is why §8.5 forbids fitting the ASCs, and why every headline must carry its sweep band. More outcome data will not fix it, which is why the next step is not harvesting.
    • ## 3. What kind of work comes next
    • - 4.2.5 (new) — the escort tour draws its destination from the education *distribution* rather than from the child being escorted, so household members never co-locate and a third of all trips cannot be carried by anyone.
    • - 4.2.6 (new) — one flat 15+ employment rate is applied to every adult, putting ~35,000 phantom elderly commuters into exactly the cohort that rides. Sequenced second because it contaminates the first's validation.
    • Runs are explicitly *not* next: the two arms cost 42 h and another would spend 30 h measuring a demand we already know is broken in two specific ways.
    • ## ⚠ 4. Four tasks proposed for deletion or rework — your call
    • | 5.2 | DELETE | a §14 toolchain change invalidates every prior run, to get pedestrian crossings on one corridor |
    • | 5.3 | REWORK — drop the site visit | one already-swept tram parameter |
    • | 6.1 | REWORK — fallback only, else report B1 untestable | elapsed *weeks* buying pedestrian counters for a secondary retail hypothesis |
    • | 6.2 | REWORK — scope to the existing land-use layer | same family, same distance from the goal |

    ## Summary Adds freight as a physically simulated truck mode. Previously the model carried no heavy vehicles: the measured 6.52% heavy share was applied at comparison time only, and the through-traffic tier's gate volumes — anchored on AADT that includes trucks — were locked entirely to car at PCE 1. Corridor road-space effects (hypothesis B3) were therefore measured without the vehicle class that consumes the most capacity per vehicle. Design record: DECISIONS.md §9.49. ## Changes - qsim: mainMode = car,truck; vehiclesSource = modeVehicleTypesFromVehiclesData with an explicit per-mode vehicles file, re-emitted per run so a swept B.freight.pce reaches the mobsim. The car type restates MATSim's default exactly (RUN.qsim.car_vehicle; verified against the shaded jar's bytecode), keeping existing car physics unchanged. The truck type carries PCE 2.0 (literature, swept 1.5–3.5) and the regulated 100 km/h cap. - Through freight: each cordon gate's volume now splits car/truck by the gate station's own observed heavy share (Hunter Expressway 0.1529 observed; 0.0652 measured-median fallback). Conservation is exact: 16,264 car + 1,691 truck = the previous 17,955

    • Adds freight as a physically simulated truck mode. Previously the model carried no heavy vehicles: the measured 6.52% heavy share was applied at comparison time only, and the through-traffic tier's gate volumes — anchored on AADT that includes trucks — were locked entirely to car at PCE 1. Corridor road-space effects (hypothesis B3) were therefore measured without the vehicle class that consumes the most capacity per vehicle.
    • Design record: DECISIONS.md §9.49.
    • - qsim: mainMode = car,truck; vehiclesSource = modeVehicleTypesFromVehiclesData with an explicit per-mode vehicles file, re-emitted per run so a swept B.freight.pce reaches the mobsim. The car type restates MATSim's default exactly (RUN.qsim.car_vehicle; verified against the shaded jar's bytecode), keeping existing car physics unchanged. The truck type carries PCE 2.0 (literature, swept 1.5–3.5) and the regulated 100 km/h cap.
    • - Through freight: each cordon gate's volume now splits car/truck by the gate station's own observed heavy share (Hunter Expressway 0.1529 observed; 0.0652 measured-median fallback). Conservation is exact: 16,264 car + 1,691 truck = the previous 17,955 through agents.
    • - Internal freight: 88,702 weekday truck trips drawn over the observed freight-industry attractor (census ANZSIC place-of-work) at B.freight.trip_ratio (assumed 0.0697, swept 0.0–0.14; zero disables the layer).
    • - New measured artefacts: heavy-vehicle hourly departure profile and weekend day factors from the classified RMS hourly counts (extract_freight_profile.py; 33,816 station-days, 12 stations; SAT 0.4627, SUN 0.4104).
    • - Smoke run (1% × 2 iterations, rc=0, accounting closes): 913 truck trips completed, 922 vehicles entered traffic, 140,380 link traversals across 28,428 links — matching the expected 1% of the generated demand.
    • - Escort binding unchanged: 121,621/177,370 bound, identical to §9.46. Week trip rate 3.383 vs HTS 3.473.
    • - Registry 316 fields, hardcoding ledger 0 under --strict, reach 74/74; check_package 1,466 checks passed; manifest 423 files; check_city_agnostic 13/13.
    • Planned comparability break: the demand family changes (through composition, freight tier, vehicles source). bind1000_25pct is the last run of the §9.46/§9.47 family; no run made after this change is comparable to it.
    • Truck routing is unconstrained (no truck-route, curfew, or bridge-limit layer exists in the package) — stated in the design record. No holdout row is read; the gate split uses the same structurally filtered calibration rows as §9.41.
    • Closes #24.

    • Records the calibration-base modelling decision (deliverable 5) and lands the machinery that will assemble it. Per DECISIONS.md §8.5, the decision is logged before any result of the current demand family exists.
    • Decision record: DECISIONS.md §9.50.
    • Stacked on #46; retargets to main when it merges.
    • Deliverable 5 takes §8.5's second admissible branch: constrain and report.
    • - The first branch (estimate ASCs on era 3/2018, hold fixed) is recorded infeasible as stated: no 2018 demand exists, the historical reconstruction was dropped, and estimating 2018 constants under a 2026 population would introduce exactly the confound §8.5 exists to prevent.
    • - The six mode constants stay at their §8.5 priors, held fixed. asc_car_passenger is not re-solved against the §9.48 occupancy excess (0.4855 vs 0.3503) — doing so would absorb a modelled defect into a behavioural constant (ASC absorption, the primary threat to validity named in proposal §9). #9 is resolved by decision; the excess is reported in the calibration record instead.
    • - No parameter search is run. After the loop fix below, the legitimately searchable set is exactly two parameters at ~21 full 25%×1000 runs (~a month of compute); neither can reach the structural misfits (§9.25/§9.28), so the search is declined with its cost stated. The loop remains built and gated for a future approved search.
    • - New: calibrate.py --constrained-base TAG assembles params/C5_calibration.json from an existing run's fit under this branch — empty search, the declined search recorded with its cost, constraint violations stated as they come out. Refuses a run without _run.json.
    • - --constrained-base exercised against a missing run (refusal path) and a real run (bind1000_25pct) — correctly surfaces the §9.48 constraint violations. The test artefact was removed; the real C5 will be assembled from a completed run of the current family.
    • - --plan verified: 2 movable parameters after the fix (was 9, of which 5 were false positives).
    • The base run for this record was stopped before completion (~iteration 20) and quarantined to results/_aborted_20260820/; deliverable 5 therefore remains open until a run of the then-current demand family completes and its fit is assembled into C5 + the calibration report. Scheduling that run is tracked in the board's task 4.5.0 — later changes on this stack alter the demand family again, so sequencing should be settled before relaunching.
    • Refs #14, #9 (they remain open until C5 exists).

    • Adds motorbike as a physically simulated mode, implementing the part of #49 that has an observed anchor. Motorbike demand is carved from car-driver demand — where both the census and the HTS place motorcyclists — so no trip is invented and the fit comparison stays consistent.
    • Design record: DECISIONS.md §9.52. Stacked on #51.
    • - The observed anchor: 653 of 179,761 core-SA1 one-method journeys to work (0.363%) are by motorbike/scooter (census G62) — the observation the earlier "declined for want of a target" position lacked. What remains assumed is the commute→all-purpose transfer: B.motorbike.trip_share = 0.0036, swept 0.0–0.01 (zero disables the mode). PCE 0.4 (literature, swept 0.3–0.75).
    • - Mechanism: a person-level carve — licensed, car-available persons become motorbike users with probability q = 0.00518 (over 426,129 eligible), drawn by a hash of person id + master seed: deterministic, identical across day types, and consuming no RNG stream, so all pre-existing draw sequences are byte-identical. The day locks to the mode via the existing generic lockedMode path (no Java change); escort days fall back to normal choice (documented collateral — the ride pairing pairs passengers with car legs).
    • - Smoke run (1% × 2, rc=0, accounting closes): 12 riders, 52 motorbike trips completed, 6,286 link traversals, zero stuck.
    • - Registry 319 fields, ledger 0 under --strict; check_package all passed; check_city_agnostic 13/13.
    • None beyond the family boundary already opened by #46 (that family has no completed run, so no additional comparability boundary is created).
    • ## Out of scope (tracked on #49)
    • The pt reporting split (tier R), choice-distinct PT submodes (tier C), and taxi/rideshare (task 4.4).
    • Refs #49, DECISIONS.md §9.52.

    ## Summary Completes physical simulation for every person-transport mode in the model: 1. Paired ride passengers physically board the driver's vehicle (JointRideEngine). 2. Walk and bike become network-simulated qsim modes (pedestrians at PCE 0.0 speed-capped at walking pace; cyclists at PCE 0.2 taking real carriageway space). 3. Unpairable ride demand re-modes to physical walk, making the ride share emergent from household driver supply instead of declared. Design records: DECISIONS.md §9.53, §9.54, §9.55.     • 1. Paired ride passengers physically board the driver's vehicle (JointRideEngine).
    • 2. Walk and bike become network-simulated qsim modes (pedestrians at PCE 0.0 speed-capped at walking pace; cyclists at PCE 0.2 taking real carriageway space).
    • 3. Unpairable ride demand re-modes to physical walk, making the ride share emergent from household driver supply instead of declared.
    • Design records: DECISIONS.md §9.53, §9.54, §9.55. Stacked on #52.
    • The ride realisation gap decomposition (#51) put the losses at ×2.24 mode co-assignment × 6.91 realised-window × 2.73 link resolution. A passenger who is *in* the vehicle makes all three layers structurally unable to fail, which selected the boarding-engine option from the design dossier.
    • ### Physical boarding (§9.53)
    • - JointRideEngine (qsim MobsimEngine + DepartureHandler, consulted before the teleportation engine via explicit component ordering): pairing stays at BeforeMobsim in RidePairingEngine (§9.44 unchanged); each paired ride leg becomes a booking redeemed at the qsim's own departure — board when the driver's car is still parked at the shared origin link (real PersonEntersVehicleEvent), alight at the shared destination. A missed boarding falls back to the previous behaviour verbatim and is counted.
    • - The car type now declares seats = B.ride.max_passengers_per_vehicle: the qsim's boarding capacity previously fell back to a built-in default of 4 that merely happened to equal the declared cap.
    • ### Network walk/bike (§9.54)
    • - Road-rule exclusions declared (walk off motorway/trunk classes; bike off motorways) with per-mode largest-SCC network cleaning (walk stripped from 16,726 unreachable links, bike 5,177 — counts reported; MATSim refuses subnetwork islands).
    • - Four teleported walk/bike registry fields retired; the measured 1.6902 walk detour factor survives in its remaining teleported role (the access/egress stub). MATSim's built-in teleported defaults cleared; the non_network_walk helper declared explicitly — including its scoring, which had been silently falling back to library defaults on every PT access leg.
    • - The transit router emits mode-walk legs with generic routes (9,466 per 1% day), which the stock agent source cannot tolerate once walk is a main mode. Two narrow qsim components carry them: TolerantAgentSource (parks vehicles only for network-routed legs; rejects any vehicles source other than the declared one) and GenericRouteTeleporter (claims generic-route main-mode departures; refuses to invent a duration).
    • ### Emergent ride (§9.55)
    • - Documented consequence: equilibrium ride is bounded by the 15.31% household OD-coincidence, below the observed 20.60%; the difference is the unobserved non-household-lift share and is reported as such.
    • - allmodes_probe (1% × 2, rc=0): final iteration ride = 67 trips, all physically boarded; walk 9,050 / bike 2,311 / car 3,785 / truck 912 / motorbike 52 trips; 2,758 unpaired ride legs re-moded at iteration 0; 4,100–4,300 PT stubs teleported per iteration. Per-mode conservation verified directly from the events.
    • - Boarding verified two independent ways: engine counters (67–71 boarded/iteration, 2–6 missed, 0 absent/full) and event analysis (71 PersonEntersVehicleEvents at the exact ride-departure second into another household member's vehicle).
    • - Registry 327 fields, ledger 0 under --strict; check_package all passed; check_city_agnostic 13/13 (the fixture test now excludes helper modes from the scored-mode vocabulary).
    • The run summariser's per-mode stuck attribution over-assigns end-of-day aborts (events conserve exactly; the attribution does not) — tracked as #54, to be fixed before the next full run so the accounting gate is trustworthy.
    • Same family boundary as the rest of this stack (no completed run exists in it). Scoring structure changes with the retirement of beeline walk/bike and vehicular access stubs (accessEgressType=none) — recorded in §9.54.
    • Refs #48, #49, #30, #28, #31.

    ## Summary Fixes #54. The run summariser's accounting closes gate false-negatived healthy runs: it took per-mode stuck counts from telemetry's in-flight tracking, which over-assigns end-of-day aborts. Accounting is now read from the final iteration's own events stream, with each stuck event attributed to the person's open leg. ## Changes - src/analyse/summarise_run.py: new events_accounting() streams output_events.xml.gz and counts per-mode departures, arrivals and stuck; a stuckAndAbort for a person with no open leg is counted in a new duplicate_aborts field instead of corrupting the conservation identity.     ## Summary Codifies two repository-process rules set on 21 August 2026: no change lands on main by direct commit, and a session's single pull request is opened at /handoff close-out — then watched to merge, with the branch deleted on both sides before the handoff counts as complete. ## Changes - .claude/CLAUDE.md: the two rules, including that pre-rule direct commits stay in history as they are (main is never rewritten; a repository ruleset blocks force-pushes regardless), with the root commit as the single structural exception. - .claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md: the Landing section now opens the PR at handoff, arms a merge watch, and completes only after merge + branch deletion; the final self-check gains a matching item. - cities/newcastle/docs/handover/NEXT_AGENT_BRIEF.md: the standing-directives list carries both rules for the next session. ## Testing - compileall, check_manifest.py, check_hardcoding.py --strict (0 items) pass. - Documentation and process only — no model, data, or registry change. ## Breaking changes None.

    • Four workstreams, executed under the project's goal directive of 21 Aug 2026 (fix the non-household-lift gap; replace assumptions with data; keep the framework city-agnostic; pursue iteration speed without any teleportation; progress every issue that does not need a converging run). Everything is probe-verified; no scenario result is produced or claimed. A new comparability family starts here (network + model + demand change; the previous family had no completed run, so the boundary is free).
    • Fixes #60.
    • Walk wedge (#60) — verified, then repaired (DECISIONS 9.58). Bytecode inspection of the pinned engine disproved the filed mechanism: the qsim never reads disallowedNextLinks (routers apply turn restrictions per mode). All 491,349 refusals were first-hop topology breaks — 6.8% of activities sat on links outside the walk/bike subnetworks, MATSim silently started routes at the nearest in-network link, and ~11.6k walk/bike legs per iteration wedged and aborted mid-day. Repairs: pedestrian exclusion corrected to motorways only (the road rules never barred trunk); one reverse walk/bike complement per one-way street (16,603 on S2; dismounted-cyclist speed = declared walking speed by identity); a new ActivityLinkAssigner pins every activity to a link carrying every network mode its person can use (config-derived, including walk for transit persons); SubtourModeChoice restricted to the person subpopulation via a declared schema restrict clause (405 external boundary agents had mode-innovated off their measured cordon counts).
    • Non-household lifts (DECISIONS 9.60, dossier docs/design/non-household-lifts.md). A booked passenger now physically waits at the meeting point for the driver's car, bounded by the declared pairing window (timeout completes on the fallback clock counted from the timeout). Unbound serve-passenger tours — generated at the observed 10–19.5% rate but unplaceable by the household binder — are re-targeted at build time to passengers in driverless households: the tour becomes driver-home -> passenger origin -> passenger destination -> home with the serving leg departing at the passenger's own departure, so the unchanged pairing rule matches it and the unchanged boarding engine physically boards it. WEEKDAY binds 55,280 of 55,614 (99.4%). Sampling co-clusters bound household pairs so the coupling survives the sample fraction. No trip is added; the ride share stays emergent; the household/non-household split is reported, never fitted (no observation of who-drives-whom exists).
    • Measurements replace assumptions (DECISIONS 9.61). The G15 census table (present in the package all along, contrary to a claim in the code) now supplies the observed per-SA1 tertiary full-time split; the classified hourly counts supply the SAT:SUN split (1.1473), the external weekend scaling (0.8429/0.7347 — the assumption 0.4/0.3 under-scaled weekend boundary demand by roughly half) and the weekend departure shift (1 h, equal to its assumption). Four assumed registry fields retired; the B2 chain-timing scaffold constants (26/16 km/h, 240 s) become declared, swept fields. B1/B2/plans regenerated on the full population.
    • Performance, measured (DECISIONS 9.59). All wall-time knobs are now declared fields; four 25% probes run one at a time measured them: replanning_threads = 20 (replanning 76 -> 33 s/iteration, the one clean win); events threads stay 4 (12 buys nothing); synchronizeOnSimSteps=false is a 65 s regression; oneThreadPerHandler crashes this MATSim build (recorded on the field); linkDynamics = PassingQ is declared on correctness (FIFO let a 1.25 m/s pedestrian hold a link's queue head against the cars behind it, contradicting the declared PCE-0 semantics) at a measured ~42 s price. The declared stack runs ~233 s/iteration at 25% (~65 h/arm); the honest answer to the 10x ask is that it is not reachable without shrinking the physical work — the available multiplier is two concurrent arms, which fit this machine.
    • Reporting (#49 Tier R) and city-agnosticism. _metrics.json gains pt_split (linked pt trips keyed by boarded submode set; boardings by bus/rail/tram/ferry; taxi/rideshare as explicit not-modelled rows) and fit.py prints every submode row; intervention patronage is attributed by the city's declared intervention.mode against each route's scheduled transportMode instead of a line-id name heuristic. The run CLIs read the scenario default and day-type vocabulary from city.json; two hardcoded EPSG transformers now use city.crs(); unlisted transit vehicle types are reported unpatched instead of silently keeping tool defaults.
    • - check_hardcoding --strict 0; check_manifest OK; compileall clean; check_city_agnostic 13/13; full check_package ALL PASSED (429 manifest files).
    • - Wedge verification probes (1%): turn refusals 3,800/iteration -> 0, before and after the demand regeneration.
    • - Lift verification probe (1%): rc=0, accounting closes, waiting counters live, the old missed-boarding classes measure 0.
    • - Timing probes phys_timing2_{base,evt,async,fifo} (25% x 5 each, sequential); a binding invariant check on the regenerated B2 (serving leg departs at the passenger's departure with identical O/D).
    • - New comparability family: nothing run after this compares to phys50_25pct, the aborted phys1000_25pct diagnostics, or anything older.
    • - #62 — make the input contract itself city-free (output schemas, layers contract, reader shapes; the audit findings the gates structurally cannot see).
    • - #63 — deliverable-0b backlog (ranked derivations, two attended acquisitions, ~25 reclassifications).
    • - The next agent's first item: bring the project the arm-relaunch decision on this family (~65 h single, or two concurrent arms).

    • Executes the 24 Aug goal (all ridership toward real-life values, ride first, all traffic forms at observed values) as far as it can go without a new converged run. The ride-choice collapse measured in the completed arms is decomposed to its mechanical causes and repaired in the demand build; the missing walk short-trip mass gets an observed distribution; freight rail is researched and scoped on observed infrastructure; two 0b assumptions become measurements; the demand package is regenerated and probe-verified.     • Ride (#48, #31 — DECISIONS §9.68)
    • - New src/analyse/decompose_ride_choice.py: of 77,626 ride-available persons, 76,986 held no ride plan in final memory and only 109 held a scored-out one — the ASC lever is exonerated. Return legs paired at 0.8% and intermediate legs at 0.0% throughout search; the uniform seed's 0.2 car probability matched the 0.196 outbound pairing ceiling.
    • - Both escort binder passes now allocate serve tours as drop-off + pick-up pairs per direct 2-leg passenger tour (B.activity.escort_binding_directions, swept). The household pass uses a pending-pickup ledger so the two serve tours may come from different household escorters; the non-household pass binds all-or-nothing with the same driver preferred.
    • - liftHousehold becomes a comma-separated list; RidePairingEngine searches all serving households; sample_population unions the full chain into one sampling cluster. New B2_escort_bindings_<day>.csv; B2_lift_bindings_<day>.csv gains direction.
    • Walk (#30 — §9.69)
    • - Two-component gravity mixture per purpose: a short kernel whose mean is the already-held observed walk trip length, with weights solved against HTS Sydney 2012/13 Table 4.4.7 distance-band shares (declared as literature, ±25%) and the long kernel re-solved so every observed per-(purpose × LGA) mean distance is preserved exactly.
    • Freight and other traffic (§9.70, #68)
    • - Hunter Valley coal trains (~110 movements/day; ARTC/PWCS/NCIG) are deliberately not simulated: they run on dedicated track grade-separated from the modelled passenger line since 2006. Recorded as a scope decision with sources.
    • - The two real road interactions — St James Rd Adamstown and Clyde St Islington level crossings — are designed as swept time-varying capacity closures and filed as #68. The Mayfield port truck cap (1,268/day) is recorded as an upper-bound constraint on the freight tier.
    • 0b measurements (#63 — §9.71)
    • - A.corridor.pre_lr_lanes_per_dir 2 → 1: Overpass attic queries (2017-01-01 pre-construction, 2016-01-01 cross-check) show every lane-tagged pre-LR corridor segment carried one lane per direction. Raw responses and provenance are committed under data/raw/osm_attic/ (ODbL).
    • - The VoT set checked against TfNSW Economic Parameter Values Jan 2025: commute/business/trip-weighted/distance-rate supported within their sweeps; education and the concession factor divergent — flagged for decision, values unchanged.
    • - src/analyse/mode_by_demographics.py delivers #50's modelled mode × age/sex/employment/licence table from arm A (children travel 46–50% by bike and ~0% by ride — the displaced-ride signature).
    • - B2, plans and all 30 run-input sets regenerated; manifest at 436 files.
    • - check_hardcoding --strict 0 · check_manifest OK · compileall clean · check_city_agnostic 13/13 · check_package ALL PASSED (2 standing warnings).

    • - B2_lift_bindings_<day>.csv gains a direction column; liftHousehold may carry multiple comma-separated household ids (older single-id populations still parse).
    • - Updated with evidence: #48, #30, #49, #50, #63. Opened: #68. None closed (the open halves await the next converged arm).

    ## Summary The approved post-repair base arm (task 4.6.9, 25% x 1000 WEEKDAY) was launched twice on 24 Aug and both process trees died silently within minutes, without any error artefact; the project then ended the campaign. This PR records the episode and brings the project record current. No model, data, registry or target value changed; the regenerated demand package (DECISIONS.md 9.68/9.69) is untouched and remains probe-verified. ## Changes - DECISIONS.md: new section 9.72 (the two launch deaths with timelines, open attribution, the operative launch constraint, and two standing directives: no run approval standing, and the conditional replication rule — arm B only if arm A's solo iterations 2-5 pace at 217-253 s/it); change-log row; topical-index row. - STATUS.md: header, blocking state, runs-on-disk (9 -> 11 aborted directories, the two new ones named with cause-stating _meta.json), open-issue count (8 -> 9), task 4.6.9 row. - NEXT_AGENT_BRIEF.md: rewritten in place — launch-blocked headline, the launch constraint and conditional replication rule as standing directives, new trap (supersedes the Start-Process detachment advice for runs), issue ledger and PR history

    summary_excerpt
    ## Summary Activates the previously inert all-modes batch as a single comparability boundary (family F6) and completes every open work item that does not require a full simulation run. After this PR, the model build is complete: every person-transport mode is physically simulated or priced, every corridor mechanism (signal timing, tram/bus priority, level-crossing closures, charging dwell, submode-distinct PT costs) is explicit and declared, and the only remaining step before new measurements is a converged run on the activated inputs. ## Changes Activation (DECISIONS 9.77, family F6) - A.signals.representation flipped to explicit_signals: all 30 run-input sets consume the generated signal plans, apply the saturation-flow capacity patch to the emitted run networks, and read the transformed transit schedules (which carry the dwell offsets and remove each variant's own embedded intersection delay). qsim.usingFastCapacityUpdate=false is emitted for signal runs. - New A.crossings.representation gate wires the freight level-crossing closures into every config as a time-variant network; RUN.travel_time.bin_size_s lowered 900 to 300 so the router can see a closure. - Taxi

    • Activates the previously inert all-modes batch as a single comparability boundary (family F6) and completes every open work item that does not require a full simulation run. After this PR, the model build is complete: every person-transport mode is physically simulated or priced, every corridor mechanism (signal timing, tram/bus priority, level-crossing closures, charging dwell, submode-distinct PT costs) is explicit and declared, and the only remaining step before new measurements is a converged run on the activated inputs.
    • Activation (DECISIONS 9.77, family F6)
    • - A.signals.representation flipped to explicit_signals: all 30 run-input sets consume the generated signal plans, apply the saturation-flow capacity patch to the emitted run networks, and read the transformed transit schedules (which carry the dwell offsets and remove each variant's own embedded intersection delay). qsim.usingFastCapacityUpdate=false is emitted for signal runs.
    • - New A.crossings.representation gate wires the freight level-crossing closures into every config as a time-variant network; RUN.travel_time.bin_size_s lowered 900 to 300 so the router can see a closure.
    • - Taxi added to the choice and routing vocabularies and to city.json: one blended priced point-to-point mode on the archived 2025 fares instrument.
    • - S3 gains bus-keyed signal priority via the declared A.signals.tsp.priority_group (corridor group in S3's overlay); the priority controller resolves the configured group instead of a hard-wired name.
    • - Family F6 declared in docs/audit/run_families.json; F5 closes with no converged arm (recorded, with the regeneration path for its inputs).
    • PT submodes (issue #49)
    • - Bus/rail/tram/ferry are score-distinct via SwissRailRaptor mode mapping, behind RUN.routing.pt_submode_scoring; per-submode constants from C1 now reach route choice. A new PtSubmodeMainModeIdentifier keeps trip-level labels at pt, preserving all existing aggregate comparisons and avoiding a crash in the stock identifier on interchange trips.
    • Registry and data (issue #63)
    • - Seven source upgrades, including B.population.bike_available_rate moved to the CWANZ 2025 NSW survey value (0.493) with the plans regenerated on it; A.signals.min_green_s cited to the published TfNSW standard; five tolerances reclassified as definitions.

    summary_excerpt
    ## Summary An /onboard gap scan found the project's front door three phases out of date. README.md advertised a 376-row manifest against 489 on disk, a 210-field registry against 356, a road network 7,070 edges short and 612,680 synthetic agents against 612,687 — and carried two statements that were false rather than merely stale: that networks/osm/ was empty and that the issue #32 re-harvest had not been run, nine days after it ran and the issue closed. STATUS.md held the same figures table and disagreed with its own P3 phase row. .claude/CLAUDE.md put the hardcoding ledger at 95 when it is 0. Every one of those numbers was correct when written, and none was wrong in a way a reader could see. The mechanism was duplication: one figures table living in two documents, and the two session skills each carrying their own copy of the six state-of-the-project questions. This corrects the figures and makes the drift class detectable, by giving documentation the same treatment check_hardcoding.py already gives code. No model or data value changed, no run was launched, no target moved, the 67/143 split is untouched, and nothing here is a result. ## Changes New check -

    • The front door described the package — 489 files, 50,182 edges, 356 fields — and said nothing about whether the model reproduces the city it models. It also described the corridor's traffic signals only as an input that could not be obtained, nine days after signal control became mechanical in every assembled run-input set.
    • The correction. The light rail's modelled patronage has been reported as a −63% error against an observed 3,417 boardings/day. fit.py marks that target unscorable and states why: March 2019 – February 2020 is a pre-pandemic PT market, PT mode share roughly halved before the 2026 base year, and V002 is V001 ÷ 30.4 rather than an independent datum. patronage.targets is empty. The modelled 1,260 is a level; the percentage was a statistic the model's own fit declines to compute. The framing had propagated through an audit document, the DECISIONS index and three consecutive handover briefs. Filed as #84, which also carries the open question this exposes: nothing currently scores the intervention's patronage at all.

Light and dark variants, no plotting dependency, and no wall-clock: a figure that restamps itself churns the diff and cannot be checked. --check therefore gates them, and check_package.py runs it.

    • Carries two sessions of work on the iteration-200 gate loop: the ninth session's two repairs (ten commits, previously unpushed) and the tenth session's measurement of them.
    • The repairs both work and neither is sufficient. Scored at iteration 150 on the quantity fit.py actually uses, one change at a time:
    • | survey category | observed | F6 unfixed | F7 (ride ratchet) | F8 (+escort coherence) |
    • | Other (bike+taxi) | 3.20 | 21.95 | 21.30 | 21.31 |
    • | Public transport | 3.80 | 7.88 | 7.70 | 7.44 |

    • | Walk only | 13.40 | 18.05 | 17.55 | 17.52 |
    • | mean abs error, pp | | 10.991 | 10.460 | 10.348 |
    • Every scored category improved across F6 → F7 → F8 and none regressed. Neither repair moved a parameter.
    • Model repairs (ninth session, DECISIONS.md §9.81 / §9.82)
    • - RidePairingEngine no longer mutates the plan when a ride leg fails to pair. It had re-moded the leg to walk directly, so pairing failure destroyed an alternative while success created none — 95.7% of the 61,409 iteration-0 misses were gone by iteration 1 and never returned. The forced walk is now an execution, restored at AfterMobsim after the events scoring reads, so the walk is still charged in full. Worth −0.531 pp of mean abs error.
    • - New EscortCoherenceListener proposes the coherent plan back to an escort pair that per-agent replanning has split; ChangeExpBeta scores it like any other plan and the driver is never touched. B.ride.escort_coherence_rate is a search rate whose zero recovers the previous behaviour exactly. Worth a further −0.112 pp. Registry 356 → 357.
    • - New probe_replanning_25pct overlay (8 iterations at 25%, innovation on through 6.4) after a 25%×2 probe proved structurally blind to replanning.
    • Measurement (tenth session, DECISIONS.md §9.83)
    • - Car is not over-chosen. It is 11.7% under (52.12 vs 59.00). The recorded "car bias" was the §12.1 geography error.
    • - fit.py folds bike and taxi into one target, so the two over-chosen modes compound into a single +18.11 pp miss.
    • - The residual is a demand ceiling, not a mode-choice defect. Every B2 trip carries party_size = 1; escort-bound travel is 5.4% of trips against an observed 20.6% vehicle-passenger share. Two measured observations agree on a ~14× shortfall: occupancy 1.0013 modelled against the measured 1.3503, and passenger share 1.61% against 20.60%.
    • - Correction to §9.82, which stays as written: its 8-iteration probe's pair-rate reversal at iterations 7–8 is the innovation cutoff (0.8 × 8 = 6.4), not convergence. The 1000-iteration arm kept falling through the same iterations.
    • - Measured and not acted on: taxi has no availability gate at all and age reaches nothing (0–4 year olds take 31.1% of trips by bike and 19.5% by taxi, bounding at 19% of the excess); gradient reaches mode choice through nothing on a network where 30.5% of 50,182 road edges exceed 4% grade.
    • - Opened #86 — synthetic demand generates 5.4% passenger travel against an observed 20.6%.
    • - Reopened #21 — gradient reaches mode choice through nothing, now measured as material rather than only recorded.
    • - Commented measured numbers on #48, #49, #50.

    quoted_numeric_lines
    • Carries two sessions of work on the P4 gate loop: the eleventh session's family F9 (joint household travel, gradient link speed, age gates), which had not been opened as a pull request, and the twelfth session's family F10, which diagnoses why every ride-pairing repair so far has been inert and repairs the cause.
    • The F9 gate-2 arm reached its iteration-100 gate with all five scored categories past the 20% bar and was stopped. F9's driver-side pass measured inert against the previous arm at equal depth (mean absolute error 10.920 → 10.864; ride 4.91 → 4.87), and that inertness located the cause.
    • The cause is a translation loss, not a mode-choice defect. All three demand binding tables name the driver — joint 70,964 rows, escort 109,971, lift 45,602 — and build_matsim_plans.py read that identity to decide *seeding* and then discarded it. Nothing in the MATSim population recorded that two people were ever a pair, so RidePairingEngine re-discovered each pair from geometry plus a 15-minute window, while MATSim's own TimeAllocationMutator moved the two members apart independently at a ±1800 s default that no registry field declared.
    • | binding | ride legs | declared driver on the same OD by car | gap median | inside the 15-minute window |
    • | joint | 28,709 | 73.8% | 10.3 min | 60.6% |
    • | escort | 26,410 | 67.4% | 23.1 min | 42.6% |
    • | lift | 7,746 | 80.5% | 7.1 min | 64.5% |
    • The driver is present, driving, making that very trip, and refused on the clock. The seeded demand is not the constraint: modestats carries ride 0.1903 at iteration 0 against an observed 0.206.
    • Family F10 (twelfth session)
    • - build_matsim_plans.py writes a boundDriver person attribute carrying the declared driver from all three binding tables — 158,898 persons. The joint table alone would have covered 46% of affected legs and left escort, the worst-affected, still identified by the clock.
    • - RUN.replanning.time_mutation_range_s is declared and swept. It had been reaching the mobsim as an undeclared framework default; the config-group name timeAllocationMutator was verified against the pinned pt2matsim-26.6-shaded.jar rather than assumed.
    • - B.ride.bound_pairing_window_min is derived from it by identity, and relaxes identification only. The inferred window stays 15 minutes and still governs every pairing the engine must infer; endpoints, vehicle capacity and physical boarding decide as before; the residual gap becomes waiting time the passenger pays for in score. A bound window narrower than the inferred one is refused, so a binding cannot become a way to buy pairings. Setting the two equal recovers F9 exactly.
    • Family F9 (eleventh session, previously unopened) — the joint-tour binder, gradient into walk and bike link travel time on both router and mobsim sides, and the taxi and bike age gates.
    • Registry 357 → 372. Ledger 0, document currency 0, city-agnostic 13/13.
    • - Validation is partial and is not a result. The 8-iteration replanning probe was stopped on instruction at iteration 2. What it established before stopping: the config parses with the new module and parameter, the run reaches iterations, and paired_by_identity is 7 at iteration 0 (no drift yet, so the mechanism is correctly inert) and 1,745 at iteration 1. Against F9 at equal depth: pair rate 0.4936 → 0.5095, occupancy 0.2770 → 0.2860, physical wait-boardings 453 → 637, wait timeouts 3,964 → 3,784.
    • No arm has reached a gate on F10, so the repair's effect on mode share is unmeasured. Nothing in this PR is a result. No target value moved, no threshold was invented, and the 67/143 holdout split is untouched.
    • - Opened #88 — taxi is routed on the network but teleported in the mobsim (39,892 of 39,923 legs per iteration, consuming no road capacity). Deliberately excluded from F10: it is a network-loading boundary and would make the pairing repair's effect unattributable. The record states explicitly that the fare *is* scored, so this is a physical-fidelity defect and not the cause of the Other excess.
    • - Commented measured evidence on #48 (ride as a physical passenger) and #86, which is re-scoped: its demand-ceiling half is answered by F9, and the realisation is what now fails.
    • The population regenerates, so nothing run on F10 compares with F9, and F9 already broke comparability with F6/F7/F8. The calibrated base remains the pre-repair F4 arm and must not be compared with either family.
    • Run the F10 arm and gate it at iteration 100 on the per-mode basis (~7.6 h at the measured 273.82 s/it). It needs a fresh stated-cost approval; none stands. Success is paired_by_identity growing with depth while the pair rate and occupancy stop decaying and ride rises as Other and walk fall.

    • The iteration-100 gate on the first arm carrying the taxi fleet fired with 9 of 11 fittable modes past 20% deviation. This PR carries what that produced: three yardstick defects fixed, two model changes measured and rejected on their own evidence, one harness correctness defect fixed, the demand's ride ceiling located and classified, and four of the session's own conclusions corrected after measurement refuted them.
    • Nothing here is a result. No arm in F10–F13 carries a _run.json, and none has ever reached its innovation cutoff.
    • - The PT composition counted another city's stop (§9.100). station_entries_exits_newcastle.csv carried a light rail stop belonging to a different city — 30,241 boardings, 15.6% of the light rail leg — while five of this line's six real stops contributed nothing. The train leg pooled 24 stations across three LGAs (53.7% in the target LGA) against a bus leg that is one contract region. The window lay entirely inside a bus series that falls 319,770 → 37,414 boardings in one month while every other region continued normally. Station membership is now derived from the city's own mapped schedule and boundary layer, the window must be contiguous and break-free, and a line reported at one stop is scaled by a measured share. Targets moved: bus 1.3039 → 2.3819, heavy rail 2.0922 → 0.7737, light rail 0.4039 → 0.6444. Heavy rail's −1.5% "fit" was an artefact of the contaminated split. +3 registry fields.
    • - Truck was scored against the wrong population (§9.101). Its target's own basis says it is *not comparable* with a person-trip share. Scored where the target was measured — the classifying count stations, calibration split only — it reads +5.4%, not −49.6%. The reader no longer prints a deviation on the wrong basis. 20 of the 24 classifying stations are holdout and were not opened.
    • - The gate now reports geometry (§9.107). mode_targets_by_mode.csv gains target_mean_km from the survey's own TRIP_AVG_DISTANCE, and the reader prints modelled mean trip length beside every share. Walk reads +852% on geometry against +89.5% on share — a distinction no share alone can make.
    • - route_contains pairing rule (§9.102): built, measured against a committed control differing in that field alone, and it does not help — pair rate 0.5069 → 0.5113 while ride share moved the wrong way. §9.92's ruling that both_links stays is confirmed by measurement rather than by the circular argument it was originally made on. Kept as a declared sweep member.
    • - Walk/bike feasibility bounds (§9.106): derived at 3.22 km and 23.95 km, they first killed the run on the subtour chain invariant, then made the fit worse (sum of absolute deviation 509.9% → 577.1%). Set to 0.0, disabled and reproducing. +2 registry fields.
    • - B.ride.unpaired_fallback (§9.105): a passenger denied a lift who holds a licence and a car now drives rather than walking 10 km. Six of seven modes moved toward target and taxi came inside the bar at +7.5% — but pt moved away (−19.6% → −30.2%) and walk's geometry barely moved. +1 field, walk reproducing.
    • - Resume matched two runs differing in a declared value (§9.104) and handed back the wrong one — find_completed compared parameters, --set overrides and the controler hash but not the resolved registry values, which is exactly where a run-config overlay sets things. A paired diagnostic would have reported a difference of zero. _run.json now carries values_sha256; records predating it do not match, by design.
    • - §9.108: read as a trend rather than a level, car, walk and pt are all converging and arrive between iterations 200 and 350, walk's geometry with them. Four repairs this session went into a transient.
    • - §9.109 / §9.111: at iteration 0, before any replanning, 42.4% of generated ride demand is unservable by the demand itself, and 69.9% of the 73,258 refused joint bindings name the companion as their own driver. driver_party_full accounts for 2, vindicating that field's own "does not bind" claim.
    • - §9.113: supply ruled out for light rail and ferry on departures (252 and 107), not on route-id day tags, which lie.
    • Four, all recorded rather than edited away: §9.107 (destination placement is not the walk defect), §9.110 (the companions' days are not full), §9.114 (most cyclists own cars, so bike is not displaced ride), §9.115 (the motorbike carve is its target times a ratio that should have cancelled).

    • The #92 candidate-pool filter was committed in b65d280 via PR #95 without its rebuild, while its own record described it as deliberately not applied. The demand on disk stayed the pre-filter demand, so the repository could not regenerate its own demand from its own code — and all eight arrival gates passed over that state, because none of them compares a builder with the artefact it produced.
    • Caught from the committed build report: candidates 201,931 with candidates_unservable absent is a report the committed builder cannot write.
    • Both queued fixes applied together, and all three day types, the MATSim plans and the 30 run-input sets rebuilt. Measured on WEEKDAY:
    • | candidates | 201,931 | 146,260 |
    • | candidates_unservable | — | 55,671 |
    • | bound | 74,663 | 82,384 |
    • | skipped_infeasible | 73,258 | 35,937 |
    • | thin_p | 0.8565 | 1.0000 |
    • | driver_is_the_companion | 51,215 | 8,150 |
    • The earlier estimate of "roughly 110,000" is superseded by the measurement: 82,384. Thinning stopped applying altogether, so joint binding is now supply-limited by servable candidates — a different regime, and a WEEKDAY property only (SAT 0.6216, SUN 0.5955).
    • B.motorbike.trip_share 0.0036 to 0.0024064, assumed to derived. The two observations behind the identity are declared rather than reachable only inside a build script, and build_mode_targets.py now asserts them against the acquired sources on every build. mode_targets_by_mode.csv is unchanged apart from line endings, confirming the carve moves generation and not the yardstick — motorbike's modelled share goes down, and that is a consistency repair, not a fit repair.
    • This opens family F14. Nothing run before compares with anything run after, including the two F4 arms the README draws its fit figures from.
    • - Three consumers claims were semantically true and textually false: each named the class that *applies* a value through a config-group accessor rather than the group that names the key. Repaired on both sides. 0 false claims remain across 193 claims over 179 fields.
    • IllegalStateException: Subtour contains a mix of chain- and non-chainbased modes had killed five arms (26, 27, 29 August and twice on 30 August) and was carried as a settled trap.
    • Three mechanisms were argued from the code and all three refuted: the reach-refusal path (the throw is inside MATSim's own strategy, and the bounds are 0.0 so it is unreachable); the car fallback for a denied lift (every restore succeeded — 48101/48101, 50705/50705, 53890/53890); and a nested-subtour conversion in the escort listener (a rebuilt arm died identically, 918 s against 928 s).
    • A two-sided diagnostic measured it instead. In one replanning round, 8 plans arrived mixed and 20 went from clean to mixed under MATSim's own strategy. The shape never varies: a degenerate one-trip child subtour — two consecutive activities within coordDistance of each other — is given a non-chain mode by probaForRandomSingleTripMode, which is valid for the child and leaves the parent holding car and pt together. The plan then sleeps in the agent's memory and kills the run only when mode choice later selects the parent. The intermittency was the signature and had been read as flakiness.
    • 1. A proposal that would leave a subtour mixed is refused and the pre-innovation plan restored whole — the principle the reach refusal already states in the same method.
    • 2. A plan that arrives mixed is stood aside from mode choice, since no draw can make it valid; ReRoute still runs. This is a refusal to crash on #96, not a repair of it.

    • Sixteenth session. Five root causes measured and fixed from the root, recorded as DECISIONS.md 9.127–9.131; families F19 and F20 opened and their arms closed out with causes; the licence rate replaced by the published count over the published population; the handover written for a machine that is idle and a data package that is half rebuilt.
    • - A run's identity includes the sha256 of the population it sampled from (inputs_sha256 in _meta.json / _run.json, declared in the output schemas), so a rebuilt demand can never resume an earlier probe (9.127).
    • Ride pairing (family F19)
    • - A declared ride pair whose links differ is served by the driver's detour: RidePairingEngine routes the driver's car leg through each carried passenger's origin and destination links, the passenger boards and alights at their own link, and the booking is at the routed pass time. New registry field B.ride.declared_pair_meeting (driver_detour | passenger_links) bound to ridePairing.declaredMeeting (9.128). A walking meeting point was built first and rejected on measurement (8–11 km walked per passenger on a 1% smoke).
    • Demand (family F20)
    • - The shared-ride binder couples a passenger to drivers in the same sampling-hash bucket (B.ride.shared_lift_hash_bucket 0.05) instead of at-or-below: the old rule kept named drivers at 12.4% and everyone else at 7.95% in a 10% sample. Measured on the binder: 73,509 servable / 59,701 bound / 0 short on WEEKDAY (9.129).
    • - The motorbike and truck carves solve their probability on the pool that is actually drawn (named drivers excluded): the rebuilt motorbike carve delivers 0.2666% of resident trips against 0.2654% solved (was 0.153%). The F20 arm read motorbike 0.378% against 0.3785% at iteration 10 (9.129).
    • - Heavy rail and light rail are held to their disclosed boardings per weekday, all travellers (light rail 2,954 from the line's Opal series; heavy rail 6,529 from 24 stations' entries), via new CAL.pt.weekday_factor; build_mode_targets.py writes pt_boardings_targets.json; report_mode_ridership.py scores modelled boardings × 1/fraction (9.130). On that basis light rail reads −44% to −51% (not −96%) and heavy rail +372% to +475%, five times over at suburban stations.
    • Population (family F21, not yet run)
    • - Acquired the TfNSW Driver Licence Statistics snapshot (2026) and the ABS population by age and LGA (2024) with provenance (cities/newcastle/extract/fetch_licences.py); build_licence_rates.py measures licence holding by age band and LGA; B.population.licence_rate_by_age_band is measured (18–24 0.78, 25–74 0.94–1.00, 75–84 0.92, 85+ 0.51, 12–17 0.08) and the population builder draws at each LGA's rate. The literature vector had left 14.2–14.8% of employed persons unlicensed; the rebuilt population has 90.8–91.7% of employed persons with a car available outside Newcastle LGA, matching the census journey-to-work structure (9.131).
    • - DECISIONS.md 9.127–9.131 with index rows and change-log rows; STATUS.md board rows and batch 4.15.27–4.15.36; NEXT_AGENT_BRIEF.md rewritten in place; run_families.json F19 and F20; overlays f19_gate_10pct and f20_gate_10pct; results/INDEX.md; registry reference and schema regenerated (414 fields); manifest 501 rows.

    ## Summary Public transport journeys are now charged the published Opal fare. Until this change the model charged car fuel, parking and the taxi meter while every train, bus, tram and ferry ride was free — asymmetric pricing no observation supports, in a model whose heavy rail read +161.8% at the F21 gate on exactly the long trips a distance-banded fare prices. The schedule is the official one, archived with provenance and declared field by field; nothing in code decides a number (DECISIONS.md 9.135). The cause was selected by measurement on the stopped F21 arm's own outputs before anything changed: heavy rail is +131% even when scored on the target's own entries basis, over at every suburban station, while Newcastle Interchange reads under; the walk/car imbalance sits inside the car-available group; ride pairing is healthy and the ceiling is bound demand; the truck and motorbike diagnostics queued by the previous brief are read and recorded. ## Changes - cities/newcastle/data/raw/fares/: five archived transportnsw.info pages with provenance_fares.json (sha256, retrieval date, values quoted verbatim); the HTML bytes stay gitignored like all raw downloads. - `cities/newc

    ## Summary Two bodies of work. First, the F22 arm: the first run of the fare-priced model (S2 x WEEKDAY, 25% x 300 by decision at approval) ran to its iteration-100 gate and was stopped under the GOAL.md loop - bus came inside its band (+8.0%), the first of the twelve modes at any gate; heavy rail fell 37,540 -> 16,512 boardings inside the arm and was still falling; the walk/car imbalance survived pt pricing (DECISIONS.md 9.136). Second, on a user directive, the results store: run bulk becomes a 500 GB budgeted cache, findings become permanent, and the run lifecycle - processing, gate stops, death marking, trimming - is automated end to end (DECISIONS.md 9.137). ## Changes - Family F22-pt-fares-priced declared at launch; overlay f22_gate_25pct; the arm's gate reading, trend and truck-stations diagnostics recorded (9.136) - No-run measurements: the motorbike carve's over-delivery is the sa1_thinned cell aggregation (+12% over the target LGA identity; draw and pool exact per LGA); the corridor attraction deficit is structural by distance band; ride decomposes generated 19.13% / bound 16.0% / realised 12.1% - src/run/results_store.py: results/raw (bulk cache, RUN.storage.raw_cap_gb

    • Two bodies of work. First, the F22 arm: the first run of the fare-priced model (S2 x WEEKDAY, 25% x 300 by decision at approval) ran to its iteration-100 gate and was stopped under the GOAL.md loop - bus came inside its band (+8.0%), the first of the twelve modes at any gate; heavy rail fell 37,540 -> 16,512 boardings inside the arm and was still falling; the walk/car imbalance survived pt pricing (DECISIONS.md 9.136). Second, on a user directive, the results store: run bulk becomes a 500 GB budgeted cache, findings become permanent, and the run lifecycle - processing, gate stops, death marking, trimming - is automated end to end (DECISIONS.md 9.137).
    • - Family F22-pt-fares-priced declared at launch; overlay f22_gate_25pct; the arm's gate reading, trend and truck-stations diagnostics recorded (9.136)
    • - No-run measurements: the motorbike carve's over-delivery is the sa1_thinned cell aggregation (+12% over the target LGA identity; draw and pool exact per LGA); the corridor attraction deficit is structural by distance band; ride decomposes generated 19.13% / bound 16.0% / realised 12.1%
    • - src/run/results_store.py: results/raw (bulk cache, RUN.storage.raw_cap_gb = 500, oldest trimmed after findings extraction, deletions logged) and results/processed (records mirrored at every transition + mode-reading snapshots, never trimmed); 122 legacy run dirs migrated, raw trimmed 748 -> 479 GiB
    • - run_matsim: runs created under raw; a gate watcher reads all twelve modes every RUN.gate.interval_iterations = 100 and stops the JVM itself on the stop bar, recording the gate table as the cause; processing and trim at harness start and run end
    • - run.py --stop NAME --cause TEXT: the one sanctioned manual stop; run_failure.py reads only the log's last 64 MiB (the whole-file read exhausted memory on a 6.9 GB log)
    • - Registry 450 -> 452 (both new fields source definition); CONFIG_REFERENCE and required_fields regenerated; board, brief and eight position pages updated; sections 9.136-9.137 appended with index and change-log rows
    • - 1% x 2 smoke through the new path: landed in raw, records and snapshots mirrored to processed unattended, rc=0
    • - The migrated layout verified: index, board, reporter and fit-figures all resolve; the F22 gate reading reproduces byte-identically through the store
    • - Issue comments posted on #98 #99 #93 #30 #86 #82 #96 #66 with the measured numbers
    • - Raw bulk older than the 500 GB budget is deleted automatically (findings retained); 35 run dirs were trimmed in the first pass (see results/processed/_trim_log.json).

    ## Summary Implements the three behaviour channels the two research artifacts (the Mode-Choice Ledger and Twenty City Twins, 31 Aug–1 Sep) ranked above everything remaining, on the user's 1 Sep goal directive. Each channel is literature-priced or derived, carries a sweep, and sits behind a registry representation gate whose absent value recovers the F22 model. Family F23-behaviour-channels is declared and its first arm is running. - Bike traffic stress (#107): every bike-capable run-network link carries a bike_stress_factor from a declared OSM-class→AADT-band mapping and Broach, Dill & Gliebe 2012 felt-distance equivalents (×1.30 / ×2.39 / ×7.68, purpose-bound sweeps). Charged in score (citysim.BikeStressScoring, felt surplus × the trip-weighted VOT identity) and applied in the router's bike link cost (citysim.BikeStressDisutility). - Parking search time: a charged parking spell in a §9.31 priced zone pays its derived search minutes once at arrival — Shoup 2006's 8.1-minute mean (swept 3.5–14) scaled by the zone's existing density-weight ramp — priced per minute at the transfer-penalty identity. Third column of parking_prices.tsv. - **Income-scaled money sensi

    • Implements the three behaviour channels the two research artifacts (the Mode-Choice Ledger and Twenty City Twins, 31 Aug–1 Sep) ranked above everything remaining, on the user's 1 Sep goal directive. Each channel is literature-priced or derived, carries a sweep, and sits behind a registry representation gate whose absent value recovers the F22 model. Family F23-behaviour-channels is declared and its first arm is running.
    • - Bike traffic stress (#107): every bike-capable run-network link carries a bike_stress_factor from a declared OSM-class→AADT-band mapping and Broach, Dill & Gliebe 2012 felt-distance equivalents (×1.30 / ×2.39 / ×7.68, purpose-bound sweeps). Charged in score (citysim.BikeStressScoring, felt surplus × the trip-weighted VOT identity) and applied in the router's bike link cost (citysim.BikeStressDisutility).
    • - Parking search time: a charged parking spell in a §9.31 priced zone pays its derived search minutes once at arrival — Shoup 2006's 8.1-minute mean (swept 3.5–14) scaled by the zone's existing density-weight ramp — priced per minute at the transfer-penalty identity. Third column of parking_prices.tsv.
    • - Income-scaled money sensitivity (#108): each resident's census G17 weekly band midpoint is stamped as the income plan attribute; MATSim core's IndividualPersonScoringParameters scales marginalUtilityOfMoney by (average/personal)^exponent (1.0, swept 0.5–1.5), with external/freight excluded and no-income persons keeping the subpopulation value.
    • Crowding disutility is deliberately deferred until fares settle rail (#98).
    • - Registry: 10 new fields (452 → 462) across A.bike_stress.*, A.parking.search_*, C.income.*, each with provenance and a sweep or held-fixed rule; CONFIG_REFERENCE.md and required_fields.json regenerated.
    • - Data: plans rebuilt (424,190 of 621,364 WEEKDAY persons carry income), 30 run-input sets reassembled (47,652 stressed links on S2), manifest regenerated (509 files, LF-normalised).
    • - Docs: DECISIONS §9.138 with index and change-log rows; board, brief and four position pages updated; family ledger gains F23-behaviour-channels (from 20260901T133356).
    • - check_hardcoding.py --strict: 0, with all new bound fields proven to reach the config.
    • - Smoke run 20260901T132710_2it_1pct (completed, _run.json): average income 1012.13 logged by the core class; iteration-0 events carry 1,139 parkingSearch and 406 bikeStress score charges.
    • - First F23 arm 20260901T133404_300it_10pct launched detached at the measured ~18–21 h pace, verified past PersonPrepareForSim into iterations, self-gating at 100/200/300.
    • - Nothing before the F23 boundary compares with anything after: the plans (income attribute) and the network (stress stamps) join the run identity.

    • Closes the fourteen defects and nine of the twelve risks the 3 September whole-repository assessment filed (#112 to #137), without a run. Each defect was verified at HEAD before it was changed; seven of the proposed fixes were corrected first (an exit code the results store would have misread, a lineage rule that would have named one city inside the framework, a date pin no live Overpass query carries, a width that would have become a compensating constant, a controller merge the two deformation models do not admit, a partial lazy-load, a reorder that would have written no status card). No model value moved, no target changed, no arm ran, no approval was spent.
    • Three issues are decisions for the user and stay open (#129, #133, #134); #131 awaits the arm for its disk measurement. The issue gate therefore stays red until those are taken, which is what GOAL.md requirement 10 asks.
    • - The gate watcher stops on the reporter's JSON verdict (--gate-json), never on the printed GATE: line the reporter also prints on a pass; a passing milestone is logged and the run continues; an unready milestone is retried every RUN.gate.retry_interval_s (300 s, declared); the log is read incrementally through one shared cache (#112, #131).
    • - The status card is written after input validation, config emission and the run-stack check; a refused launch writes a failed card quoting the refusal and retires the directory (#127).
    • - run.py --stop and --list no longer need a valid registry; the sampler and the summariser load it on first use (#126).
    • - java resolves by platform, the JVM pid is recorded and --stop kills it; the README states that --detach is Windows Task Scheduler (#128).
    • - Trim keeps a completed run whose metrics are not extracted and runs on a daemon thread after the launch; a processed twin left under a run's pre-abort name is reconciled; a hand-named run resolves through its own record (#132, #137).
    • - Refused taxi trips are restored by re-finding the trip by endpoints through a helper shared with the ride engine, replacing the whole trip and consuming each once (#113).
    • - SCATS priority takes an extension from a stage after the tram's and a recall from the running stage before it; a last-in-cycle tram stage is refused, counted and logged; the conditional lateness boundary matches the fixed-time controller (#125).
    • - The resolver refuses a derived_from naming a missing field, a self-reference, a numeric value outside its own sweep (dict values leaf by leaf, or the entries a new sweep_keys names), an overlay value outside a categorical sweep, and a named run overlay that is absent; check_city cross-checks B.seed.master and asserts every consumers path exists (#123, #124). Three registry breaks repaired.
    • - New fields: CAL.pt.censored_cell_value (0, swept 0 to 25) read by the mode-target builder (#129); RUN.gate.retry_interval_s.
    • - The HTS extract, the Opal bus slice (matched on the contract declared in schedules/operators.json), the scenario-config writer and the corridor pedestrian-phase flag reproduce their committed artefacts; the dead S2a call is removed and the schedule report states the delta (#115, #116, #119, #120, #121).
    • - The manifest reads every provenance record recursively in both forms; every row carries a licence resolved from the city's declared sources and derived_licences (161 ODbL, 337 CC-BY 4.0, 0 blank); check_manifest.py refuses a blank; every processed row's producer is asserted to exist and to name its artefact, with 24 file-level producers declared (#117).
    • - The Overpass harvester writes a provenance record; the existing harvest gets one marked reconstructed; the third mirror is allowlisted; the DEM fetch refuses instead of a typed rectangle (#118).
    • - The board prints no deviation beside level only or representation and the shape check refuses one (#114); the replay page imports the city module (#122).
    • - CI runs on main pushes and pull requests, pins Python 3.14, fails on a trivial record, and runs the configuration-reference and legacy-drift checks (#130).
    • - Six record headings normalised, seven index rows added (#135); README launch rules, package size pinned to the manifest, five words (#136); the calibration report names the base run by its directory (#137).
    • - Record section 9.141, six position pages, the board and the brief.
    • - python tests/check_package.py: ALL CHECKS PASSED at 512 manifest files, 420 processed rows with a producer that names them; one warn (the bike beeline factor outside its IQR sweep, pending a decision on re-measuring C2).
    • - Producers re-run and diffed against the committed artefacts: HTS, Opal bus slice, scenario tables and mode targets byte-identical modulo line endings; corridor layer moves 65 of 70 rows as intended.
    • - controler_sha256 changes with the Java, so no arm launched after this compares with one launched before. Family F24 is declared at its first launch and none has run, so nothing on disk is affected.

    ## Summary Takes the three decisions that were holding the launcher under GOAL.md requirement 10, repairs the corridor's missing CBD end at its cause, re-measures the network circuity factors on the network that actually runs, and profiles an iteration's wall clock for the first time. No arm was launched, no approval was spent, no target value changed, and the 67/143 validation split is untouched. Family F24 is declared at its first launch. ## Changes ### Destination choice is constrained at both ends (#30) A gravity model solved against an observed mean distance constrains production only: every origin sends the right number of trips the right average distance, and nothing requires a destination to *receive* the share of arrivals its own attraction states.
