    quoted_numeric_lines
    • Takes the three decisions that were holding the launcher under GOAL.md requirement 10, repairs the corridor's missing CBD end at its cause, re-measures the network circuity factors on the network that actually runs, and profiles an iteration's wall clock for the first time.
    • No arm was launched, no approval was spent, no target value changed, and the 67/143 validation split is untouched. Family F24 is declared at its first launch.
    • ### Destination choice is constrained at both ends (#30)
    • | worst zone's arrival share against its own attraction share, work | 12.87 | 0.007 |
    • | the same, shopping | 34.66 | 0.37 |
    • | the same, other | 9.62 | 0.010 |
    • | the CBD SA2's share of non-home work trip ends, against attraction | — | 1.02x |
    • | the same, shopping | 0.59x | 0.99x |
    • | the same, other | 0.69x | 0.99x |
    • The attraction vector itself was right — the published place-of-work count puts 8.24 % of core jobs in that SA2 against the 8.27 % the layer assigns it, and the 2011 journey-to-work table puts 9.09 % of core-to-core commutes there. The *draw* was free to ignore it, which is why the shortfall widened with distance and why three families of pricing and behaviour repairs could not move light rail or heavy rail. Shopping is the one purpose whose worst-zone gap does not reach the declared tolerance: one destination multiplier cannot match a two-component mixture, which is recorded with its reason rather than papered over by raising the iteration cap.
    • The draw is now balanced at the destination end as well (Wilson 1967; the Furness/IPF balancing of the classical four-step model), solved jointly with the decays because balancing moves the realised mean distance. This introduces no new observation, constant or tunable: the destination multiplier is the multiplier of a constraint the attraction vector had already declared. B.activity.destination_balancing = singly_constrained reproduces the previous build exactly, so the pair is comparable by construction.
    • - #129 — censored patronage cells. Decided by measuring first: the package holds *one* censored cell, outside the series the heavy-rail target sums, so the field's sweep moves no target at either end. The exclusion of censored cells from the holdout station means is recorded as the pre-registered treatment of those rows rather than unified, because the target is a sum over stations and the holdout figure is a mean over station-months. Three build guards now hold that decision to its measured premise, and all three were exercised.
    • - #134 — declared sweeps that are never run. The registry used one word for two things: a reported sensitivity curve and an honesty bracket. sweep_role enters the field schema with answer / uncertainty / measurement; all 255 swept fields carry a role (11 / 222 / 22), 44 missing bases were written, and the resolver now refuses a swept field without a role or an assumed sweep without a basis.
    • - #133 — no unit-test layer. tests/unit/ with 89 pytest tests over the functions that decide correctness, plus two more Java probes in the existing idiom rather than JUnit (a test framework in the pinned stack would be a toolchain change). The new fare probe immediately measured a latent defect: a Long age attribute was charged the adult fare where an Integer age is charged the child fare.
    • C2 was still measured on the network as it stood before the 16 August rebuild. Re-measured and kept, with the demand rebuilt on it: detour 1.3376 → 1.3276 (595 routed pairs, was 551), walk beeline 1.6902 → 1.6938, bike 1.5231 → 1.5570. The package check's beeline assertion is a hard check again rather than a warning.
    • From the last arm's own stopwatch.csv at iterations 101–103 (673–684 s each):
    • | beforeMobsimListeners | 402–404 | 60 % |
    • | mobsim | 193–198 | 29 % |
    • | replanning | 42–46 | 7 % |
    • | prepareForMobsim | 25–27 | 4 % |
    • | iterationEndsListeners | 3–7 | 1 % |
    • That 60 % is the ride-pairing engine's before-mobsim pass, to within a second of its own logged elapsed time. The cause was one call inside a per-segment loop, constructing about 51,600 trip routers per iteration on a single thread; the same call was also the whole of a 164 GiB-per-run log storm of one repeated warning. Both are now repaired and measured on a 1 % probe:
    • | ride-pairing pass, per iteration | 2,868 ms | 300 ms |
    • | matsim.log bytes | 13,991,606 | 285,943 |
    • | routing warnings logged | 17,375 | 0 |
    • Projected at 25 %: an iteration of about 280 to 320 seconds against the 673 to 684 measured, so a 300-iteration arm costs roughly 24 hours rather than 45 to 50, and its log volume falls from about 164 GiB to about 3 GiB. The projection is from a 1 % probe; nothing above 1 % by 2 iterations was run, and the next arm measures the real pace.
    • Eight further repairs in this project's own event handlers are proven result-preserving rather than argued: the build carrying all of them produced a pairing report byte-identical to a baseline run, the same iteration-0 event multiset and the same mode statistics. Only the router hoist changes results, because MATSim's randomising route search draws a new generator per router construction; that one item is the family boundary.
    • Establishing the standard those repairs would be judged against measured it. Three runs of one unmodified build, same package and same declared seed, produced 5,620,710 / 5,620,410 / 5,620,710 iteration-0 events, and every pair diverges by iteration 2. MATSim's shared random-generator counter is unsynchronised and the run uses 20 threads, so a handful of agents receive different routes. Mode shares were identical across all three, so a gate reading is not at risk.
    • - python -m pytest -q tests/unit — 89 passed
    • Family F24 is a comparability boundary on three counts at once — the demand (balanced destinations, re-measured circuity), the plans built from it, and the compiled controler. No run before it compares with any run after it. Nothing is lost, because no F24 arm has run.

    ## Summary Two arms ran and were read. **F25 falsifies the demand-side explanation for the ride deficit**: three repairs put 60,273 + 33,832 more bound trips into plan memory and removed 17,740 physically impossible bookings, raising the seeded ride share 31 % — and the realised share did not move (−42.5 % → −43.1 %). Being in plan memory is necessary and not sufficient, so the ride ceiling is downstream of the choice set. The arm's own pairing telemetry locates what remains: 21.7 % of selected ride legs never pair, and the rest is selection. Also built, and the reason both readings are citable at all: **a run that ends at a defined boundary now closes itself out.** A gate stop is no longer an orphan directory. Nothing here is a result: no run since family F4 has carried ran_to_last_iteration at a gate horizon. No target value changed and the 67/143 holdout split is untouched. ## Changes The run record — a run that reached its declared last iteration, was stopped by the gate watcher, or was stopped through --stop writes _run.json, _summary.json, SUMMARY.md and extracts its findings. A run that crashed still writes none. A required-on-write completion field

Measured on the F25 package before the change: **6,165 WEEKDAY escort bindings across 5,426 drivers and 3,154 lift bindings across 2,697 drivers** named a driver whose household owns no vehicle, and because the plans builder holds a serving tour at car only when a car is available, those drivers then took the variant's base mode — **85,993 non-car legs sat on a trip the same person's own boundDriveTrips declared them to drive**. A seeded plan is not a proposal, so the runtime gate that refuses this never saw it: MATSim could execute a plan in which the declared driver walked and the passenger bound to them had no driver to pair with. Issue #142 left the repair open between two readings, to be settled by a measurement on the committed package.     • Three gate readings in one session (families F26, F27, F28), four physical roots fixed with a control member each, the iteration cut from 384 s to a median 260 s, and family F29 built on a demand where the shared-ride pass can finally place its lifts on the long trips that are lifts in real life.     • History check before any patch (DECISIONS.md 9.145). The board had posed "widen the pairing window" as the next decision. The code exempts a declared pair from the clock, so miss_window never described one; ride_pairing.csv gains miss_declared_absent (appended last), and the window refusal of 9.98 stands.
    • F26 gate (9.146): 8 modes out. miss_declared_absent 719 of 77,399 — the declared pairs hold; 12,461 selected ride legs sat on persons the demand never bound, proposed by EscortCoherenceListener by inference while the gate refused 192,000 of the same kind; 12,317 car legs began while every car the household owns was already out; 571 bound trips were made in a carve lock's mode. Fixes, each with a control reproducing F26: B.ride.coherence_scope = declared; B.population.vehicle_roster = census (householdVehicles stamped on every household member, HouseholdVehicleRoster maps drivers to hh<id>_car<k>, TolerantAgentSource parks a shared car once, JointRideEngine boards into the mapped car); the motorbike and truck carves never draw a bound passenger, in the pool solve and at the draw.
    • Iteration cost (9.147): a milestone cost twice a plain iteration (plans dump, events inside the mobsim, experienced plans). RUN.controler.write_trips_interval = 10 carries the monitoring; plans and events move to 100 (the gate); RidePairingEngine routes detours on global.numberOfThreads workers, applied in order (41 s → 2 s); RUN.machine.threads 10 → 16 on the first probe of the mobsim's own thread count.
    • A global wait strands every non-chain mode (9.148): the first F27 arm under RUN.qsim.vehicle_behavior = wait stranded walk and taxi (55,862 car agents stuck at iteration 0) and was stopped at 19; its family is declared readings: none and the board skips it.     ## Summary A whole-repository assessment was produced at 419b0da and lodged as a dated report, then 29 of the 34 defects it found were closed. No scenario ran, no demand or network input moved, and no comparability family opened — F29 is still built and unlaunched. The assessment found 95 findings (34 defects, 37 risks, 24 smells), each with a file:line and a failure scenario. The pattern was not bad code; it was a gap between what a check asserts and what it can see. None of the 34 defects would have failed CI. The single most serious: the holdout was informing the calibration targets. The heavy-vehicle share that converts 31 of 34 calibration count targets to a light-vehicle basis was a median over all 23 classified stations, 20 of which are holdout — and the artefact printed its own contradiction (stations_observed 23, calibration_stations_observed 3) from the day it was written. ## Changes The 67/143 split, enforced where it was crossed - build_validation_targets.py derives the heavy share from calibration stations only, and refuses rather than falling back if none is classified. heavy_vehicle_share 0.0652 → 0.1120, sweep unchanged.     • A whole-repository assessment was produced at 419b0da and lodged as a dated report, then 29 of the 34 defects it found were closed. No scenario ran, no demand or network input moved, and no comparability family opened — F29 is still built and unlaunched.
    • The assessment found 95 findings (34 defects, 37 risks, 24 smells), each with a file:line and a failure scenario. The pattern was not bad code; it was a gap between what a check asserts and what it can see. None of the 34 defects would have failed CI.
    • The single most serious: the holdout was informing the calibration targets. The heavy-vehicle share that converts 31 of 34 calibration count targets to a light-vehicle basis was a median over all 23 classified stations, 20 of which are holdout — and the artefact printed its own contradiction (stations_observed 23, calibration_stations_observed 3) from the day it was written.
    • The 67/143 split, enforced where it was crossed
    • - build_validation_targets.py derives the heavy share from calibration stations only, and refuses rather than falling back if none is classified. heavy_vehicle_share 0.0652 → 0.1120, sweep unchanged. A target *conversion* moved, deliberately.
    • - vehicles_per_leg now declares every road mode's vehicle contribution (car 1, motorbike 1, taxi 1; ride 0, truck 0, bike 0, walk 0) and extract_metrics reads that declaration instead of naming a mode list. Previously the modelled side summed vol_car alone against a light-vehicle observation, biasing every count error low.
    • - extract_legacy_constants.py walked tree.body only — no in-function constant could ever be reported. Now walks any depth; surfaced six real items (five copies of the Earth's mean radius, one spatial-index cell size), each now a STRUCTURAL exception with its reason. Back at 0 having actually looked.
    • - A.fare.off_peak_all_day_day_types replaces day != 'WEEKDAY'. Registry 471 → 472.
    • - Metrics are extracted for any run carrying a completion, not only rc = 0 — two gate-stopped arms currently hold 336 GiB of a 500 GiB cache for want of a _metrics.json.
    • - The board printed the highest it.N on disk (101) against the record's reached_iteration (100).
    • - --truck-stations read the roster's hh<hid>_car<k> as mode car1, dropping every roster car from the road denominator.
    • - gate-pr-on-docs.sh matched gh pr create on Bash only, so the MCP create_pull_request path opened a PR entirely ungated; and its cd … || exit 0 failed open. Both fixed, all four paths tested.
    • Also: --seed bound only the numpy RNG while three hash-based decisions read the module constant; the B2 report counted legs before three binder passes rewrote the file (2,189,888 reported against 2,225,838 on disk); solve_asc_ride looked for runs under a path the store abandoned in §9.137; check_legacy_drift compared zero fields and printed "registry and source constants agree".
    • - Unit tests 108 → 118; tests/unit/test_stop_run.py pins the stop marker's reading and the task a stop may end, including the sibling arm it must not touch.
    • - check_hardcoding --strict 0 (30 structural exceptions, was 24). check_registry_rules pass. check_city_agnostic PASS 13. check_city --all PASS 40. check_manifest OK, 512 files. Document currency 0 drifted, document shape 0 problems, board blocks current.
    • - tests/check_package.py was NOT re-run — the C3 artefact and the manifest changed after it last passed. It is the first item in the brief's §0.
    • - heavy_vehicle_share 0.0652 → 0.1120, and the modelled side of the same comparison changed basis. Counts scored before this change are not comparable with counts scored after it. #82's −91.8 % should be re-read at the F29 gate rather than carried forward; the issue carries the measurement.
    • - issues gated — #147–#151 were filed for the five defects deliberately left open. Four need a ruling, one is a data job; none is labelled awaiting-run because none is waiting on a measurement, so the gate blocks a launch. That is GOAL.md requirement 10 working, not failing. Two of them (#150, #151) open a family and are therefore cheaper to fix *before* the F29 arm than after it.
    • Five defects, each recorded in §9.150 with its reason and filed as an issue: the duplicated HTS purpose map (#147, opens a family), four typed network-layer fallbacks (#148, needs a decision), 430 manifest rows with no source (#149, a data job), and two Java defects — the escort listener's hash-order RNG (#150) and RunTelemetry's missing memory barrier (#151) — which change results and could not be compiled here because .tools/ is absent.
    • The chains were not rebuilt: the B2 report fix is a reporting change, and the F29 package on disk is the one the next arm runs.

    • Rules on and closes the five defects the 7 September assessment left open (#147–#151), which had been blocking every launch under GOAL.md requirement 10; fixes a toolchain gate that was green on a checkout that could not run; and records F30's first arm, which ran healthy and was stopped at iteration 23 on its own cost.
    • Four of the five defects moved no run value. The fifth does, and family F30-an-escort-is-priced-as-an-escort opens on it alone.
    • The five rulings (§9.151)
    • - #147 — the HTS purpose map existed twice and disagreed on Serve passenger. The demand generated it as HX (its own tour purpose since §9.15) while the run-input assembler folded it into NHB and fed that to scoring_from_c1(). One shared map now (src/build/hts_purpose.py), HX wins. The repair exposed a second half: C.vot.by_purpose was still keyed on the old vocabulary, so the HX weight matched no key, was dropped from the value-of-time average and the rest renormalised — moving the collapse 16.96 → 17.317 AUD/h against a C.vot.trip_weighted declared at 16.96. Re-keyed NHB → HX at the same 15.2: renamed, not revalued. PURPOSES in build_params.py was a second copy of those keys and is now list(VOT). Measured: 140 of the 141 files under scenarios/matsim/ came back byte-identical, so the disagreement changed no number the model ever scored.
    • - #150 — a seeded draw made in hash order. EscortCoherenceListener consumed a seeded RNG while iterating a HashMap of households, so the draw was assigned in hash order of the key set — the order the sample fraction changes, which made a 1 % probe unable to predict a 25 % arm on that path. byHousehold is a TreeMap. This moves results and is the sole basis of the F30 boundary.
    • - #148 — four typed network fallbacks. Declared as A.road.speed_unknown_class_kmh, A.road.lanes_unknown_class, A.road.capacity_unknown_class_veh_hr_lane, A.active.footway_width_unknown_class_m, each with the sweep of the class table it stands in for, and stamped imputed_fallback rather than sharing imputed_rule. Measured: the three road fallbacks fire on 0 of 50,182 road edges; the footway one on 830 of 40,195 active edges. No value moved, no artefact rebuilt.
    • - #151 — RunTelemetry has no memory barrier of its own. Its arrays and maps are written from event-handler threads and read from the QSim thread with no volatile, synchronized or concurrent type; a committed overlay disables the sim-step barrier they rely on. RUN.machine.telemetry_requires_simstep_barrier is declared and run_matsim.refuse_unsafe_telemetry() refuses the combination before the JVM and in the dry run, rather than putting atomics on the event path for a probe whose barrier-off path is a measured regression (§9.59).
    • - #149 — derived provenance. build_manifest.py resolves a derived file's source from its lineage — each producing script's referenced paths, followed through processed intermediates to their raw ancestors, then to the declared sources — instead of leaving it blank; a raw file with no record of its own inherits its directory's record. source 82 → 508 of 512, source_url 80 → 499, retrieved 59 → 443. fetch_gtfs.py records a retrieval date for a feed it downloads and preserves the earlier one for a feed it skips.
    • The toolchain gate (§9.152)
    • F30's first arm (§9.153)
    • Ran from 15:08, stopped by the operator at iteration 23. Healthy — iteration 0 passed every control — and stopped on cost alone: median_iteration_s 376.42 against the 260 s its approval was priced on, which puts 300 iterations near 31 h against ~22 h. The 45 % is not diagnosed; three candidates are named and none is measured. §9.150's --stop rebuild is tested against a live arm for the first time and held.
    • DECISIONS.md §9.151, §9.152, §9.153 with their index and change-log rows; six position pages consolidated; the board's hand lines rewritten and its blocks regenerated; the brief rewritten from the template.
    • - python src/run/session_gate.py — 17/17 PASS, toolchain and issue gate included
    • - python tests/check_package.py — ALL CHECKS PASSED (2 pre-existing warnings)
    • - python -m pytest tests — 125 passed (118 before; three new modules cover the telemetry refusal, the single purpose map and the ordered draw)
    • - python src/registry/check_hardcoding.py --strict — 0, unchanged
    • - Java run stack compiles clean against the pinned JDK 25.0.4; signals stack 201 jars
    • - run.py --run-config phys_timing2_async_25pct --dry-run is refused; --run-config smoke --dry-run resolves
    • - Family F30-an-escort-is-priced-as-an-escort opens on the escort listener's draw order. Nothing run before this boundary compares with anything after it. F29 never ran an arm, so nothing is stranded.
    • - overlays/runs/phys_timing2_async_25pct.json can no longer run. It sets events_synchronize_on_simsteps false, which is now refused while telemetry depends on the barrier. Declaring RUN.machine.telemetry_requires_simstep_barrier false, together with making that state concurrent, is the way back.
    • - Registry 472 → 477 fields; CONFIG_REFERENCE.md and required_fields.json regenerated.
    • - No target value changed, the 67/143 holdout was not opened, and nothing here is a result: the last gate reading remains F28's at iteration 100.

    ## Summary The iteration is decomposed to the method for the first time, from inside the JVM rather than from MATSim's stopwatch, and a third of it turned out to be this project's own code re-deriving per link what never changes. Per-link tables cut a plain probe iteration from 310 to 205.5 s and startup from **13m47s to 7m00s** on two probes of one overlay on one machine, with our share of a plain iteration's CPU falling from 50.0 % to 14.5 %. The tables are proved identical to the formula over 3,266,754 comparisons rather than by a diff two runs cannot support. Separately, a declared value was found to reach nothing: RUN.travel_time.analysed_modes is ["car"], MATSim consults it only when travelTimeCalculator.filterModes is true, and that parameter was never emitted — so every pedestrian, cyclist, bus and truck on the network fed the single link travel-time table the car router reads (#154). A new check enumerates what else the framework decides undeclared: 31 unreviewed (#155). The 2-minute iteration the directive asked for is not reached — about 190 s unprofiled against 120 — and the remainder is measured to be MATSim's own A*, its events pipeline and a mobs

    • The 2-minute iteration the directive asked for is answered, and the answer is no — answered with arithmetic before a knob was turned, then confirmed by a probe that falsified the largest apparent lever. Alongside it, the fifth whole-repository assessment is lodged, the recommendations worth taking are taken, one is refused after checking, and four operations a session used to do by hand are now scripts.
    • No target value changed, no arm ran to a gate, no comparability family opened, the 67/143 holdout is untouched, and nothing here is a reading of the city.
    • ### The 2-minute target, priced out
    • A plain 25 % iteration is 205.5 s profiled / ~190 s unprofiled, of which the mobsim is 143 s. So if every phase outside the mobsim went to zero the iteration would still land above 120 s, and all three measured levers taken at their *full CPU share* — threads (saturated, §9.147), the events pipeline, the time-variant network — land it near 171 s. Reaching 120 s would take linkDynamics=FIFO or teleported walk/bike, both already refused (§9.59; GOAL requirement 1).
    • The §9.154 flight recording put 11.6 % of all CPU in one LinkedBlockingQueue.offer → signalNotEmpty → AbstractQueuedSynchronizer.release inside SimStepParallelEventsManagerImpl$ProcessEventsRunnable — a chain, not a fan-out, so an event pays N lock-protected hops for N threads. The knob's measured points did not bracket it: 1 was saturated (§9.56), 12 bought nothing over 4 (§9.59), and 2 had never been run.
    • f30_evt2_probe_25pct changes that one value and nothing else. 20260907T233540_4it_25pct (ran_to_last_iteration) against 20260907T192715_4it_25pct, plain iterations 2–3:
    • | phase (median s) | 4 threads | 2 threads | delta |
    • | mobsim | 143.0 | 226.0 | +58.0 % |
    • | iteration | 205.5 | 297.0 | +44.5 % |
    • The queueing is therefore not waste to be recovered but the price of keeping each stage short enough not to throttle the 16 qsim threads. 4 now stands on evidence from both sides. The knob is verified identity-free (§9.56), so the probe opened no family.
    • Bounded for next time: timeVariantNetwork makes all 143,891 links TimeVariantLinkImpl, each paying a synchronized binary search, to represent 2,441 change events on 16 links.
    • - A stopped run's bulk stops being untrimmable. The #132 guard kept any raw directory with a _run.json and no _metrics.json — which an operator or gate stop never gets, since run.py writes that file after run() returns. Measured: 13 directories, 72.8 GiB, 16 % of a 90 %-full cache, all already mirrored into processed, while the store deleted *younger complete* runs instead. RUN.storage.extract_grace_s = 3600 bounds the window. The space is not freed today (the store is under cap) — it becomes reclaimable at the next trim that needs it.
    • - The charging dwell's baseline point is declared (#157, filed and closed here — it needs no run, and under GOAL requirement 10 that means it is fixed before the next arm; filing it turned the issue gate red until it was). A.lightrail.dwell_charging_s stays unobtained; the baseline the layer is built from is now its own swept field. The rebuilt layer is byte-identical — git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol over data/processed/corridor/ is empty.
    • - RUN.storage.raw_cap_gb's units corrected to gibibytes (the code multiplies by 2³⁰).
    • fit.py:148 was reported as a defect — the patronage scorer "structurally empty". The dead used/errs locals are a clarity smell, but the behaviour is correct and documented: _fit.json reports patronage n=0 beside 32 listed unscorable targets each with its reason (§12.1). The gap is surfaced, not hidden.
    • session_gate.py --fix (regenerates every stale generated artefact and re-checks; never touches prose), src/analyse/compare_runs.py (refuses comparisons across a family, a fraction, or a profiled/unprofiled pair), src/run/verify_launch.py (performs the #70 check the launcher used to print), and arm_cost.py now says when it is pricing on a stale run — it was quoting 26.3 h off a pre-repair arm while silently excluding four newer probes.
    • docs/reports/20260907T231739_project_report.html at f40d332: 21 defects, 64 risks, 46 smells. Both research lanes re-searched not one stored row — all 46 project and 12 platform rows were inside their horizons, so the whole 56-call budget went to the library's own gaps and both stopped on the two-empty-rounds rule. MATSim's licence gap closed (GNU GPL, per its own pom.xml). Ladder recounts 7/9/24/6/0 over 46 projects; the per-mode rung is still empty for everyone.
    • - python src/run/session_gate.py — 18 / 18 PASS, including the toolchain.
    • - python tests/check_package.py — ALL CHECKS PASSED (2 pre-existing warns).
    • - python -m pytest tests/unit — 139 passed (was 125). Two new files: test_trim_grace.py pins both the leak and the #132 race it must not re-open; test_compare_runs.py pins the blockers.
    • - check_hardcoding.py --strict TOTAL 0; check_doc_currency.py --strict 0 drifted.
    • - Registry 480 → 482, manifest 512 unchanged.

Opens family F31-the-car-router-reads-only-cars and launches its first arm under a stated-cost approval.     • Applies five of the fifth project assessment's eighteen recommendations, refuses two after checking, and fixes a sixth defect that the first of them uncovered. Opens family F31-the-car-router-reads-only-cars and launches its first arm under a stated-cost approval.
    • The largest item is the price an operator is asked to approve. arm_cost.py quoted the next 300-iteration arm at 31.5 h; it now quotes 18.2 h bottom / 21.8 h top, with the iteration-100 gate at 6.1 h. The difference is not a new optimisation — it is that the pricer was measuring the wrong thing twice over.
    • The arm is priced on the iteration it repeats. arm_cost.py used median_iteration_s, a median over every iteration a run ran. On a short probe most of those are iterations an arm pays once: iteration 0 warms the JIT, dump all plans fires at iterations 0 and 1 only, and the last iteration writes the final output. On 20260908T014214_4it_25pct that is three of five iterations, and the median read 282.6 s against a recurring 216.0 s (iterations 2 and 3, at 213 s and 219 s; the one-offs cost 326 s, 282 s and 350 s). The pricer now reads the run's own output/stopwatch.csv, prices the recurring iterations, carries the one-offs once each, and warns when the run it priced never reached a milestone iteration and therefore cannot have priced one, naming the newest long arm as the top of the band. This is the same class of error compare_runs.py was taught to flag in the previous session, left in the one tool that sets what an operator approves.
    • An unprofiled pricing probe is now an overlay (f30_plain_probe_25pct) rather than something a session improvises: the profiling probe with the flight recorder and GC log off and nothing else changed, so its clock is the arm's own. It opens no family.
    • A log guard that had never once done what it said. NetworkDirectWalkPtRouter counted in plain int instance fields, but its Guice binding — addRoutingModuleBinding(pt).toProvider(RouterProvider) — carries no scope, so a new router and a new set of counters is built for every routing thread in every iteration. Its "log the first 3" sample wrote 19,469 lines on the F28 arm (about 36 % of that run's log), 4,766 on F30's stopped arm and 716 on a 4-iteration probe, while its decided % 100000 progress line fired 0 times in any run in the project's history. Run-lifetime atomics, with the progress line evaluated before the branch that returns the walk. Measured on the next run: 3 sample lines, and the progress line firing for the first time.
    • Licence boundary. Forty manifest rows carried CC-BY 4.0 beside byte-identical ODbL content: the 30 per-day-type transit schedules under scenarios/matsim/ carry 357,893 OpenStreetMap route link references, and the 10 parking_prices.tsv tables are keyed on network link_id. Both are derivative databases of OSM. Declared in the city's own derived_licences globs, so the framework still names no artefact of any city. Manifest ODbL rows 161 → 201.
    • Toolchain. pt2matsim was the one component fetched with no expected digest — it passed None where the JDK and Maven pass theirs — so its recorded pin described what arrived rather than what was expected. Pinned to the jar every mapped schedule in this package was built with. test.yml gains permissions: contents: read for its nine jobs.
    • A stale rationale. RUN.monitor.stall_s keeps its value of 300 and loses a false reason: it justified itself by "the slowest iteration measured (56.4 s at 25 %)" against a ~216 s iteration today. Re-anchored to what actually keeps the log warm — MemoryObserver's measured 60 s heartbeat — so it does not go stale again when the pace moves.
    • Family F31-the-car-router-reads-only-cars, opened at the arm. RUN.travel_time.filter_modes = true reaches a run for the first time: until now the single link travel-time table MATSim binds as the observed travel time for every network mode was fed by every vehicle on the network and read by the car router. The controler was also recompiled, which is a boundary by the project's own rule even though the recompile is logging-only.
    • Switching on the tram priority controller. Ranked as "the shortest distance between existing code and a number on the board". A.lightrail.tsp_enabled has sweep_role: answer and *is* the S2b intervention — the corridor swing S2b exists to measure. Turning it on in the base would put the intervention inside the base and close light rail's gap with precisely the compensating constant the project's calibration loop forbids. The fidelity question underneath it — whether the real corridor operates priority today — is real, is separate, is source: assumed, and is an operator decision.
    • Moving build wall time out of the hashed set. The stated benefit was that check_manifest.py would stop churning. It cannot: the record already establishes that ~18 % of pt2matsim route link sequences differ between identical builds, so the report's hash churns on the mapping itself and the wall time is dominated noise. Regenerating the artefact would also re-run the mapper, which the one-build-per-comparison rule forbids.
    • Inheriting licence from the computed ancestry for the other 129 rows. Measured, that would relabel 169 rows rather than 40, because a producing script's inputs are credited to every output it writes: bus_monthly_series.csv, a TfNSW patronage series, is credited with the buildings, parking, signals and POI extracts, while the single-purpose C2_osm_defaults.json is correct. Filed as #159 rather than guessed — inheriting from that ancestry would give the licence column the defect the source column already has.
    • - python src/run/session_gate.py — 17 of 18 lines PASS; toolchain is SKIPPED because an arm is running, and issues gated is RED on #159 by design (see Breaking changes).
    • - python tests/check_doc_currency.py --strict — 0 drifted claims. python tests/check_doc_shape.py --strict — 0 shape problems.
    • - python -m pytest tests/unit -q — 147 passed (139 before). Two new files: test_direct_walk_counters.py and test_plain_iteration_pace.py, both verified to fail against the pre-fix source rather than merely passing against the new one.
    • - python tests/check_manifest.py — 512 files verified after the licence change.
    • - python src/setup/bootstrap_toolchain.py --verify — toolchain OK against the new pt2matsim pin.
    • - The router fix is verified on a live run, not only in tests: 20260908T014214_4it_25pct wrote 3 sample lines and fired the progress line, against 19,469 and 0 on the F28 arm.
    • Family boundary. Nothing that ran before 20260908T095937 compares with anything after it.
    • The issue gate is deliberately red. #159 was filed this session and is not awaiting-run, because it can be fixed without a run — so by GOAL requirement 10 it blocks the launcher. The operator chose to file it and launch the arm with --allow-open-issues, on the ground that the defect is in how the manifest *describes* ancestry and is not something the arm measures around. This is the first deliberate override of that requirement and it is recorded in the run and in the record. It was not resolved by labelling the issue awaiting-run, which would have been false.

    • Position pages. ride-and-pairing (placement solved, the gap is volume), monitoring-and-gates (the router statistic confirmed at run scale; the counter repair held in production; the watcher's fourth live firing), runs-and-economics (the quoted band held and the point did not), sampling-and-families (F31's arm stopped at its gate).

Ride is −7.830 pp; the modes beating it total +9.500 pp. A pro-rata recovery of ride's deficit would land car at +0.9 %, bus at +9.6 % and motorbike at +2.4 % — three modes inside 10 %. That is an arithmetic upper bound on what ride volume alone can do, not a prediction.

    summary_excerpt
    ## Summary A full project assessment was produced (docs/reports/20260908T192638_project_report.html), and its recommendations were then implemented. The assessment's finding was that this project does not have a calibration loop that is converging slowly. It had no working loop at all. The automated search could reach 5 registry fields of 482, two of them taxi-only, and the single mode constant among them belonged to taxi — the one mode with no independent target. Its objective contained four folded numbers against a twelve-mode goal. And its execute path was broken, so it had never completed a single candidate. The tool said so itself: *"refusing to fit 5 parameters to 4 independent numbers: that is not a calibration."* Separately, and not previously known: a gate-stopped arm could never be read. MATSim writes output_trips only at controler end, so extract_metrics failed on every arm since F4 — which is every arm this project produces — and no gate arm had ever had a _fit.json. Both are fixed. Nothing here is a result: no arm was launched, no approval was sought or spent, and no target value changed. ## Changes The objective now measures the goal.

    • A full project assessment was produced (docs/reports/20260908T192638_project_report.html), and its recommendations were then implemented.
    • The assessment's finding was that this project does not have a calibration loop that is converging slowly. It had no working loop at all. The automated search could reach 5 registry fields of 482, two of them taxi-only, and the single mode constant among them belonged to taxi — the one mode with no independent target. Its objective contained four folded numbers against a twelve-mode goal. And its execute path was broken, so it had never completed a single candidate. The tool said so itself: *"refusing to fit 5 parameters to 4 independent numbers: that is not a calibration."*
    • Separately, and not previously known: a gate-stopped arm could never be read. MATSim writes output_trips only at controler end, so extract_metrics failed on every arm since F4 — which is every arm this project produces — and no gate arm had ever had a _fit.json.
    • The objective now measures the goal. CAL.objective.components was a *mean* over five *folded* survey categories in percentage points; GOAL.md requirement 7 is a *maximum* over twelve *unfolded* modes in relative per cent. Heavy rail and light rail sit in one folded "Public transport" cell with opposite signs, so a search could improve the old objective while making both worse. It is now goal_modes.max_abs_rel_pct, computed by calling the board's own reader, so the objective and the gate cannot drift apart. independent_targets 4 → 10.
    • The search can run. --set → --config-set (registry channel, sweep-validated, held-fixed refused). A declared matsim_param binding is now evidence of run-time realisability, so the movable set is 5 → 21 and reaches ride, taxi and bike — three of the seven failing modes, where before it reached none. The run_inputs stage was listed as implemented and carried out by nothing; evaluate() now re-assembles per candidate off the already-mapped schedule and restores the shipped assembly.
    • A stopped arm is read at the iteration it reached — the policy §9.143 already stated, implemented. _metrics.json records where each table came from. output_links has no per-iteration counterpart, so the counts block reports itself unavailable rather than substituting a different basis.
    • The reading point cannot score a candidate, and the loop now refuses. Measured within-run across all six 25% arms that reached iteration 100: the objective drifts 0.272–0.418 pp, upward on every arm, and the worst scored mode moves 15.72–24.88 points — wider than the 10% band itself. CAL.search.reading_drift_pct is measured; convergence_delta is derived from it; --execute refuses while the drift exceeds the pass band and names the remedy as changing the *reading*, not the rule.
    • The PT routing failure is diagnosed. Of 2,553,357 routing requests, 33.4% get no transit route and 40.6% of the answered take the network walk — three in five come back as a walk. Access radius, search parameters and schedule integrity are refuted; time of day accounts for ~4 points. The cause is pricing: one second walking costs 1.0400 seconds riding. The raptor's cost carries no mode constant, no fare and no distance term, so the submode split is decided on travel time alone.
    • Three mode constants opened, two created, each with a per-mode reason; heavy rail, ride and walk stay frozen because their deviations are a missing mechanism, a volume deficit and a routing failure respectively. The §8.5 departure is argued in the record before any run reads them.
    • Lineage is resolved per output (#159, closed). OSM in source under CC-BY 129 → 0; ODbL without an OSM ancestor 21 → 0; undetermined 512 → 0, ratcheted. A new check fails on disagreement in either direction and found a live breach on its first run.
    • - session_gate.py: 17 of 18 PASS. issues gated fails — see Breaking changes.
    • - check_manifest.py: 512 row(s) agree, 0 undetermined (cap 0) · OK
    • - check_hardcoding.py --strict: TOTAL 0 · check_doc_currency.py --strict: TOTAL 0 drifted claim(s) (50 claims)
    • - check_doc_shape.py --strict: TOTAL 0 · build_status_board.py --check: BOARD current
    • - check_city.py --all: PASS 67 FAIL 0 · check_city_agnostic.py: PASS 13 FAIL 0
    • - pytest tests/unit -q: 204 passed · compileall: clean · toolchain compile: PASS
    • - End to end on a real arm: aborted_20260908T100009_300it_25pct is the first gate arm in the project's history to carry a _fit.json. Its twelve deviations reproduce the board exactly, objective 247.2131 on heavy rail, is_a_result: false.
    • The issue gate is red, honestly, for the first time. It required only a label, so requirement 10 was satisfiable trivially and forever — while a real defect was left unfiled because filing it would block the launcher. It now requires an AWAITING-RUN: <measurement> line. Twelve issues were given a real measurement; the gate went 16 → 3 blocking, then to 5 because two further honest non-run defects were filed. The five need an operator decision, not a code change: #49 and #50 are standing directives no single run settles, #155 waits on 31 accept-or-declare decisions, and #164/#165 are defects found and not fixed. The override is now first-class, refused without a stated reason, and counted.
    • Two claims in an earlier assessment are corrected here on measurement: standingRoomInPersons is not 0 (bus 44/18, ferry 149/51, rail 98/48), and motorbike's constant is not swept because motorbike is not a choice alternative.

    ## Summary Three issues worked to a close and one large negative finding. The remedy that DECISIONS.md §9.158 proposed for the calibration reading point — averaging a window of iterations instead of reading a single one — was built, declared, measured against the same six arms, and found to be worse than the point reading it replaces. The cause retires the approach rather than tuning it: the movement it was meant to average away is a monotone trend, not noise, and a mean over a monotone series is its centre. Alongside that, the two issues that were blocking the session gate were closed by doing the work, and the teleported public-transport access leg (#167) was filed and fixed at the router, with the one remaining gap measured and named. No arm was launched.     • Three issues worked to a close and one large negative finding. The remedy that DECISIONS.md §9.158 proposed for the calibration reading point — averaging a window of iterations instead of reading a single one — was built, declared, measured against the same six arms, and found to be worse than the point reading it replaces. The cause retires the approach rather than tuning it: the movement it was meant to average away is a monotone trend, not noise, and a mean over a monotone series is its centre.
    • Alongside that, the two issues that were blocking the session gate were closed by doing the work, and the teleported public-transport access leg (#167) was filed and fixed at the router, with the one remaining gap measured and named.
    • No arm was launched. No target value changed, no demand or network was rebuilt, and the 67/143 validation holdout is untouched.
    • ### The reading point (#163)
    • - CAL.gate.reading_window_iterations declared (40 iterations, sweep [20, 80], bracket stated), with report_mode_ridership.report_window built inside the one reader the board, the gate watcher and the calibration objective all call, so those three cannot read different quantities.
    • - Measured over the same six 25% arms, within each run: heavy rail 41.46 deviation points against the point reading's 24.88, bike 4/6 arms → 6/6, four modes past the whole 10% acceptance band instead of three, objective drift 0.081–0.5395 pp and still one-signed on every arm.
    • - Every scored mode's series over iterations 40–100 is monotone without a single reversal (car 59.78 → 66.94, walk 14.55 → 9.76, bike 6.23 → 4.66, heavy rail 27,948 → 19,140). The field stays declared, and its own description records that it is measured not to work.
    • ### Storage (#164, closed)
    • - Both un-closed-out arms extracted through the store's own process(extract=True), 4.0 and 3.8 minutes; their findings verified against the eleven position-page lines citing them before anything was deleted.
    • - 336.4 GiB reclaimed. Raw store 467.1 GiB (93.4% of cap) → 130.7 GiB (26.1%).
    • - results_store gains reclaim(), report() and a CLI. trim() reclaims oldest-first and only while over cap, which is why two reclaimable arms sat in a 93.4%-full store waiting for a threshold whose crossing would have happened during the next long arm.
    • ### Licence boundary (#165, closed)
    • - Content pass over all 111 networks/matsim/* manifest rows. 110 confirmed ODbL on their own content; the 15 mapped-schedule transitVehicles.xml.gz move to CC-BY 4.0, on the evidence that the assembled copies cut from them were already CC-BY — the package was labelling a derived copy freer than its own source.
    • - Ancestry moved with the licence in build_matsim_network.py's OUTPUT_INPUTS. 512 rows agree, 0 undetermined; licences 279 CC-BY / 218 ODbL plus 15 bespoke.
    • - The split is now pinned in check_doc_currency, and four existing claims found silently skipping on a wrong document path were re-aimed (50 → 54 live claims).
    • ### PT access and egress legs (#167, filed)
    • - Measured: the raptor accepts intermodal access/egress alongside the mode mapping this scenario depends on, and teleported legs fall from 520,385 to 6. The mobsim then refuses the landing link — 675 of 4,123 stop facilities (16.4%) sit on a link walk cannot use. accessEgressModeToLink fails at PersonPrepareForSim on 40 agents.
    • - DECISIONS.md §9.159 with its index row and change-log row; four position pages rewritten; the board and the brief rewritten; README and CONFIG_REFERENCE regenerated for 494 registry fields.
    • - python src/run/session_gate.py — all 18 checks pass, including issues gated, which is green in its unscoped view for the first time: 20 open issues, every one awaiting a stated measurement, 0 blocking.
    • - python tests/check_manifest.py — 512 rows, lineage and licence agree in both directions, 0 undetermined.
    • - python src/registry/check_hardcoding.py --strict — 0 items.
    • - python tests/check_doc_currency.py --strict — 54 live claims, 0 drifted.
    • - Two 1% four-iteration smoke probes ran and are readings of nothing; both are recorded with their causes.
    • None to the shipped model. The emitted MATSim config is unchanged: access_egress_basis ships at beeline, so useIntermodalAccessEgress is not emitted and routing.accessEgressType stays none. The registry gains 5 fields (489 → 494) and the manifest's licence split moves 264/233 → 279/218 with row count unchanged at 512.

    ## Summary The seventh whole-repository assessment, the fixes it named, and the first arm since 21 August that is permitted to run past iteration 100. The assessment's finding reframes the calibration effort. RUN.mode_choice.modes makes pt one alternative; which submode an agent rides is decided downstream by SwissRailRaptor, whose cost carries no mode constant, no fare and no distance term. So bus, heavy rail, light rail and ferry — four of the seven modes past the stop bar, failing in opposite directions — have no control variable in the layer that decides them. A whole-file pass over the F31 arm's plan memory (154,347 persons) measures the only channel a scoring constant does have: 974 agents, 0.63 % of the population, hold plans that differ in which pt submode they use. The search method was never the binding constraint. GOAL.md requirement 8 also gets a derived answer for the first time — the system settles about iteration 200–210 — with three falsifiable predictions the arm now running tests directly. Three checks were found green on prose describing themselves, and are fixed. ## Changes The report — `docs/reports/20260909T003402_project_report

RUN.mode_choice.modes makes pt one alternative; which submode an agent rides is decided downstream by SwissRailRaptor, whose cost carries no mode constant, no fare and no distance term. So bus, heavy rail, light rail and ferry — four of the seven modes past the stop bar, failing in opposite directions — have no control variable in the layer that decides them. A whole-file pass over the F31 arm's plan memory (154,347 persons) measures the only channel a scoring constant does have: 974 agents, 0.63 % of the population, hold plans that differ in which pt submode they use. The search method was never the binding constraint.
    • GOAL.md requirement 8 also gets a derived answer for the first time — the system settles about iteration 200–210 — with three falsifiable predictions the arm now running tests directly.
    • The report — docs/reports/20260909T003402_project_report.html, 15 sections, read at 781cf41. The standing reference library is refreshed by both research lanes, which re-searched not one stored row across 52 calls: 48 of 49 project rows and all 79 factor literature halves were carried in, and the budget went to this pass's new question. Field survey now 49 projects / 12 platforms / 14 calibration methods; factor ledger IN 45 · PARTIAL 27 · INERT 2 · ASC 1 · OUT 8 over 83 rows, with five carried factors changing class — the first movement the library has recorded.
    • The launch gate stops passing on prose about itself. src/run/issue_gate.py read *"0 blocking"* while three issues opened *"This issue BLOCKS the launcher"*. Three separate routes, all closed: its allowed-prefix class admitted a backtick, so ` AWAITING-RUN: inside a code span — how every document here refers to the convention rather than invokes it — matched as an invocation, capturing the sentence explaining why writing one would be inventing a measurement; its own documentation matched its own regex, capturing the literal <measurement>; and evidence()` returned the first match, so a discharged statement outlived its supersession.
    • Requirement 10 gains a third state. An issue may declare it awaits something other than a run — a decision, an acquisition, a mechanism — and say what, via decision-needed / awaiting-implementation plus an AWAITING-DECISION: line. Reported at every gate and launch; never blocking. No new label: the tracker already had both and no open issue used either. The gate now reads 21 open, 16 awaiting a run with a stated measurement, 5 awaiting a decision, 0 blocking.
    • The lane is declared, not scraped. lane() ran #(\d+) over an overlay's prose, so default_25pct — what a bare python run.py selects — had a lane of {5} from the sentence "issue #5 re-measures relaxation". Prose also cannot read a negation: writing "#167 is deliberately not in this lane" put it back in. Overlays gain answers_issues.
    • The calibration loop can find the candidate it paid for. evaluate() sends --config-set; _run.json recorded the raw --set channel; find_run matched that, so a candidate recorded overrides: {} and the loop raised *after a full arm's wall clock*. Its shipped test asserted "'--config-set'" in src — the sending half only. Now delegated to run_matsim.find_completed, which searches all three stores, requires ran_to_last_iteration and compares values_sha256. _run.json gains registry_overrides.
    • The §8.5 departure reaches the search it was logged for. rebuild_stage followed a matsim_param binding but not a derived_from identity, so C.asc.bus and C.asc.light_rail — opened at §9.158 specifically so a search could reach them — were still excluded as "no declared consumer". Movable set 21 → 24, gaining those two and C.transfer.beta_transfer_penalty_min. Making a field reachable is not permission to fit it: held_fixed, placeholder, --only and the independent-targets guard all still refuse.
    • A false consumer claim becomes visible on the diff. check_package.py's consumers check is local-only and needs 2.3 GiB, and was red at HEAD on two claims added the day before. Corrected, and moved into src/registry/check_city.py, which CI runs.

On that re-priced quote the depth arm 20260909T015217_300it_25pct launched at 22.3 h against its approved 32 h ceiling, and was verified into iteration 0.

    ## Summary The two things the seventh assessment named and left open, both decided by the operator and taken here: an approved cost ceiling that nothing enforced, and #167's unexplained accessEgressModeToLink failure. ## Changes An approved cost ceiling is enforced by the runner (#169). No RUN.* field declared a wall-clock limit and nothing read one, so the only mechanism that ever stopped an arm was start_gate_watch — which stops on a *modelling* condition and knows nothing about clocks. The arm running now disables that watcher by a scoped and correct departure, so it launched with no automatic stop of any kind, on deviation or on cost, for twenty hours. - RUN.gate.wall_ceiling_h, 0 = no ceiling by default — the idiom RUN.gate.interval_iterations already uses — so nothing changes for a run that names none. - RUN.gate.ceiling_poll_s (60 s), declared like the gate watcher's retry interval rather than left as a constant in code; it bounds only how far past its ceiling a run can get. - start_ceiling_watch beside start_gate_watch as a second watcher, never a branch of it: RUN.gate.interval_iterations = 0 must keep meaning *"do not judge my modes"*

    • The two things the seventh assessment named and left open, both decided by the operator and taken here: an approved cost ceiling that nothing enforced, and #167's unexplained accessEgressModeToLink failure.
    • An approved cost ceiling is enforced by the runner (#169). No RUN.* field declared a wall-clock limit and nothing read one, so the only mechanism that ever stopped an arm was start_gate_watch — which stops on a *modelling* condition and knows nothing about clocks. The arm running now disables that watcher by a scoped and correct departure, so it launched with no automatic stop of any kind, on deviation or on cost, for twenty hours.
    • - RUN.gate.wall_ceiling_h, 0 = no ceiling by default — the idiom RUN.gate.interval_iterations already uses — so nothing changes for a run that names none.
    • - RUN.gate.ceiling_poll_s (60 s), declared like the gate watcher's retry interval rather than left as a constant in code; it bounds only how far past its ceiling a run can get.
    • - start_ceiling_watch beside start_gate_watch as a second watcher, never a branch of it: RUN.gate.interval_iterations = 0 must keep meaning *"do not judge my modes"* and never *"do not enforce my budget"*.
    • - It stops through the marker path §9.143 established — written before anything is killed — and carries its own completion, stopped_at_ceiling, added to the output schema's enum and the board's state mapping, because a run stopped on cost is a different boundary from one stopped at a gate or by a person. _stop_marker reads gate, then ceiling, then operator, so a run that hit both is described by the more informative boundary.
    • #167 is diagnosed, and the cause is in our plans rather than in MATSim. Read from aborted_20260908T232051_4it_1pct's own plans.xml.gz: zero lines mention routingMode, there are no interaction activities, and every trip in the input is a single leg. So no input trip has mixed routing modes — the mixture is created inside PersonPrepareForSim, which under accessEgressModeToLink inserts walk access and egress legs and, with no declared routing mode to inherit, lets MATSim infer each leg's from its own mode (walk beside a car main leg) and then rejects the trip it has just built. The same invariant is already recorded from the other direction at RidePairingEngine.java:1193-1198, where a restored leg left on walk beside ride siblings killed arm 20260826T053741 with the identical message.
    • Documents. §9.161 with its topical-index and §14 rows; runs-and-economics and public-transport-and-yardsticks rewritten to the current truth; the board's Next and the brief re-aimed. Registry 494 → 496 fields, and every document that states that count moved with it.
    • - python -m pytest tests/unit -q — 240 passed, including test_ceiling_watch.py (7): the watcher is driven against a fake process with a clock already past its ceiling and asserted on the kill, the marker, the completion, a ceiling not yet reached leaving the run alone, a gate breach being described before a budget, zero starting no thread at all, and the completion being in the output schema.
    • - python src/registry/check_hardcoding.py --strict — 0. The poll cadence was flagged when it was a module constant and is now a declared field, which is what its siblings are.
    • - python tests/check_doc_currency.py --strict — 0 drifted; python tests/check_doc_shape.py --strict — 0.
    • None to the model, the data or any target value. No demand or network was rebuilt and the 67/143 holdout is untouched; family F32-crowding-reaches-scoring is unaffected and the running arm is undisturbed.
    • The ceiling watcher is built and not proven on a run, and the arm running now launched before it existed — its 32 h approval is still enforced by hand.

    ## Summary The depth arm 20260909T015217_300it_25pct executed the horizon it declared — completion ran_to_last_iteration at iteration 300, rc 0, 21.5 h wall against a 22.3 h quote and a 32 h approved ceiling. It is the first run since 21 August to do so, and the first _fit.json in the project carrying is_a_result: true. It relaxes, and relaxing makes the fit worse: 0 of 12 modes inside 10 % and 8 past the 20 % stop bar, against 1 of 12 inside at the gate reading that preceded it. The cause is measurable. When innovation switches off at iteration 240 every agent settles onto its best remembered plan, and car jumps +2.211 pp in one step while walk falls 0.941, taxi 0.583 and ride 0.489. That snap is the distance between the behaviour the search was sampling and the plans agents already held — so every gate reading this project has taken was of a model whose own preference was more car-heavy than the mixture it was executing. MATSim writes modeChoiceCoverage1x.txt on every arm this project has ever run, and no module read it. A scoring constant reallocates between plans an agent already holds, so a mode's plan-holding coverage is an upper bound on its share — and on the landed result 20260909T015217_300it_25pct at iteration 300, ride's target of 20.6000 % of resident linked trips sits above the 20.05 % of agents who have ever held a ride plan, against a 12.1553 % share. No value of any constant closes ride's −41.0 %. It is a choice-set finding, not a taste, and it settles a question issues #48 and #86 had circled since August. The same table dates the search: every mode's choice set is within one percentage point of its final coverage by iteration 5–10 and stops moving by 16–27 — except pt, still opening at iteration 233 and reaching only 25.78 %.     • data/processed/validation/count_station_links.csv keys stations to MATSim link ids, which are re-issued on every network rebuild. Regenerated against the network it is scored on: 197 rows, all matched by name, 0 unresolved. The same run then reads counts at mean +16.30 %, median −1.1 %, 0 modelled-zero stations, against −89.35 % / −98.7 % / 7 before. The ×1/fraction fold and the network volume were correct throughout. check_package.py gains check 7b: every mapped link must resolve on an assembled scenario network and still carry the road name the map recorded.
    • - RUN.replanning.score_msa_representation (absent | at_innovation_cutoff, shipped absent) and its computed companion RUN.replanning.score_msa_fraction, bound to scoring.fractionOfIterationsToStartScoreMSA. Until now every plan in every arm carried the score of its last execution. At absent the builder emits the literal MATSim's own parameter dump records for its default, so declaring it was byte-neutral; at at_innovation_cutoff it emits the innovation cutoff already declared, introducing no new number.     ## Summary Every open issue is now closed, awaiting one paired arm with a stated measurement, or awaiting one stated decision — and no arm ran to get there. The session spent under five minutes of JVM on four 1 % structural probes, and no approval was sought or spent. That asymmetry was measured — of 20,902 declared escort pairs, 10,224 had the passenger driving their own car — and it is the only layer that can reach ride's target at all, since 20.6000 % sits above the 20.05 % of agents who have ever held a ride plan.     ## Summary F33's first arm, 20260910T222830_300it_25pct, threw OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space in the replanning of iteration 98 after 97 completed iterations and 6.5 h. The cause was a defect in the overlay, not the model: it copied the landed arm's horizon and gate departure and not its 40 GB heap, so it inherited the registry's 14 GB while the landed arm had peaked at 36.2 GB. write_plans_interval is 100, so no plans checkpoint exists past iteration 1 and nothing warm-starts. This lands the corrected overlay, the record of what happened, and one harness fix the failure exposed. Nothing was relaunched — the operator chose to hand off, and no approval stands. ## Changes - f33_baseline_25pct.json states RUN.machine.xmx = 40g, with the reason written on it. A four-iteration pricing probe prices time and cannot price heap, which grows with plan memory over the first hundred iterations. - run_matsim.reconcile_stale() asks the run's own log before blaming a dead harness.     • The eighth project report, the issues it found filed and groomed, and every defect fixable without a run fixed — so that the next session's only lane is relaunching F33's arm 0. The report (cities/newcastle/docs/reports/20260911T210144_project_report.html) is the first rendered from the review lanes' JSON by a script rather than written by hand; its audit of its own series found 76 of 105 prior recommendations taken and the goal count unmoved, because what was taken was instruments and every model-side control they produced is built and unrun.
    • - The heap rule RUN.machine.xmx carried as prose is two declared fields (RUN.machine.heap_floor_gib, heap_per_fraction_gib); the launcher refuses a heap below it (31.4 GiB at 25 %). Arm 0 died on the 14 g default.
    • - A log silent for RUN.gate.stall_kill_s (1800 s) stops the run with the new stopped_at_stall boundary; arm 0 spent 13.1 h of its 20.9 h inside one iteration with the machine awake (Task Scheduler log, read for the first time).
    • - RUN.machine.gc_log defaults on; a warm start re-derives the innovation fraction so the cutoff iteration is preserved (the jar's arithmetic moved it 240 → 260 at N = 100).
    • - A run overlay or --config-set that, put back to its registry value, changes neither the emitted config nor the vehicle types is refused before the JVM starts. All 66 committed overlays pass; A.parking.search_min_max is refused.
    • Model-side defects (F33 has no reading, so the recompile costs nothing measured)
    • - The nine C.asc.* constants reach the emitted config from the registry at every launch instead of from the built C1_parameters.json table — --config-set C.asc.bus=… was recorded and never executed. Byte-identical for the shipped values.
    • - EscortCoherenceListener.trim() removes plans through MATSim's injected removal selector, so RUN.replanning.plan_selector_for_removal switches both removal paths (#174). GatedSubtourModeChoice treats a plan whose decomposition throws as mixed.
    • - Pt boardings are counted from MATSim's legs table at every iteration (the experienced plans carry the in-progress legs of stuck agents); light rail reads 1,224 on the landed result, the basis fit.py scores. The disclosed-station filter matches the station name whole.
    • - build_matsim_network.py unpacks the two values require() returns (it could not run since 25 August); the chains report's top-level dropped-tour count is summed; an unapplied lane patch is counted.
    • - The mobility-impairment draw is declared as four registry fields (registry 514 → 521), the builder evaluating the same expression.
    • - /project-report gains a simplification lens, the twelve-mode and supply-fidelity tables, an audit of the report series, the issue ledger (past/present/upcoming), an 80-word index headline, render_report.py, and a cadence rule (one report per reading).
    • - DECISIONS.md §9.166, its index row and its §14 row (which points past §9.165's "6.5 h"); the board and the brief rewritten; thirteen position pages stamped.
    • Issues: #180–#192 filed (the consolidations held for after the F33 pairs by decision, the footpath and crossing decisions, the acquisitions, the telemetry and ride-engine risks, the scanner, the holdout sum, test coverage, the warm-completed-arm rule); #50, #66, #86, #98, #107, #154, #172, #174 groomed on evidence.
    • - python src/run/session_gate.py — 18/18 PASS (manifest, compile, hardcoding strict, doc currency, doc shape, board blocks, city contract, schema, city-agnostic, dead runs, gate watcher, launch refusal, registry rules, matsim defaults strict, 349 unit tests, fit figures, issues gated, toolchain).
    • - New tests: the heap rule and stall watcher (13), plan removal through one selector (4), an override reaching the run (5) on real resolutions.
    • - python run.py --run-config f33_baseline_25pct --dry-run resolves with the new fields; the emitted constants equal the C1 table to the digit.
    • - The reader reproduces 5,305 disclosed-station rail boardings on the landed result under the anchored match.
    • - A run overlay that changes nothing the run reads is now refused at launch; taxi_fare_stress_1pct still passes (its fares are derived at launch).

    summary_excerpt
    ## Summary Every defect, risk and smell of the eighth project report and every open issue it filed (#180–#192) is fixed or awaiting a run. The pt access, egress and transfer walks are network legs the simulation executes (#167); the MATSim network is rebuilt with the 40,203 harvested footway ways as walk- and bike-capable links and every feed re-mapped once (#183), opening comparability family F34; the level crossings carry the 2012 Cobbora survey's freight movements (#184); TfNSW's Opal Patronage and BOAM series and BITRE registrations enter the package (#185); the four large consolidations (#180, #181, #182, #191) land with byte-identical outputs. Arm 0 (f34_baseline_25pct) is not launched: no stated-cost approval stands. Recorded in DECISIONS.md §9.167. ## Changes - #167 — the accessEgressModeToLink refusal was the ride and taxi engines re-moding one leg of a five-leg trip at PrepareForMobsim, not MATSim's pre-simulation pass. RemodeRestore.remodeTrip replaces a trip whole; NetworkDirectWalkPtRouter routes the raptor's transfer beelines; RUN.routing.access_egress_type = accessEgressModeToLink, RUN.transit_router.access_egress_basis = network.     • - Comparability family F34 opens at the rebuild (20260912T062457): nothing run before it compares with anything after it. Every scenario's mapped network and run-input set changed.

    summary_excerpt
    ## Summary Arm 0 of the calibration campaign was about to be launched on a 21.7 h quote priced on a run that executed a different controler and stalled. A 4-iteration 25 % pricing probe on the footpath network measured the recurring iteration at 555.5 s (244.5 s on the road graph), and a JFR profile put 54 % of CPU in routing with a quarter of every sample under MATSim's PersonPrepareForSim: it re-routes a person's whole plan, every plan they hold, whenever one leg has no route, and the taxi engine left one on every refused request (~48,000 an iteration at fleet 200) and on every restored taxi leg. The engines now route the trip they re-mode and restore the original; family F35 opens at that controler; its probe reads 460.0 s (−17 %), and arm 0 is running under a 44 h ceiling on a 39.0 h quote. ## Changes - src/java/citysim/RemodeRestore.java: Remode jobs routed on global.numberOfThreads workers with the run's TripRouter (departure time as PlanRouter computes it), applied in refusal order, the replaced elements kept; restoreOriginal puts the original trip back. remodeTrip removed with its last caller. - TaxiFleetEngine, RidePairingEngine: route refused / unpa

    ## Summary Arm 0 of family F35 (20260912T202242_300it_25pct, 300 iterations at 25 %) ran to its last iteration in 30.35 h and is read as the project's second result: 2 of 12 modes inside 10 % (car +9.6 %, motorbike −5.6 %), six past the 20 % stop bar, ride's target above its own 19.11 % choice-set coverage. The ninth project report is lodged, and its no-run findings are fixed: the mode reader had been resolving every run's transit stops through the city's assembled schedule, which the footpath rebuild overwrote, so the only earlier result read heavy rail 0 on the board while its own fit record said +225 %. The iteration horizon is declared at 250 on arm 0's measured drift. No arm was launched and no approval stands. ## Changes - Reader: extract_metrics.schedule_path reads a run's own output/output_transitSchedule.xml.gz first and falls back to the config path, with a warning, only for a run that never reached its end. The freight_train row counts the scheduled closures plus the freight closures the run itself carried. The innovation cutoff is computed as MATSim does (from firstIteration) by one shared function. A boardings reading with no sample fraction is refused;

    ## Summary The run viewer's map moves from Leaflet to MapLibre GL 5.24.0. Tiles are fetched and decoded in web workers and the package basemap and the loaded links are GL layers painted by the GPU, so a pan or a zoom never waits on a load or a redraw. A 3D view raises key-free terrain and building extrusions with the overlays draped onto them; the map is a globe when zoomed out; the controls follow a map app's. The typed initial centre and latitude are gone (#220). No model value, target, family or run changed (DECISIONS.md 9.173). ## Changes - src/analyse/run_view.html: MapLibre GL host replaces the Leaflet host - Esri Canvas / imagery / label rasters as sources; coast, water, green, sand, roads, rail and tram from basemap.json and the congested links from hotspot.json as GeoJSON sources with data-driven paint (delay colour, volume width and opacity, worst on top); metre-true road widths and per-class appearance zooms computed from the study latitude the basemap or the run supplies.     • The run viewer's map moves from Leaflet to MapLibre GL 5.24.0. Tiles are fetched and decoded in web workers and the package basemap and the loaded links are GL layers painted by the GPU, so a pan or a zoom never waits on a load or a redraw. A 3D view raises key-free terrain and building extrusions with the overlays draped onto them; the map is a globe when zoomed out; the controls follow a map app's. The typed initial centre and latitude are gone (#220). No model value, target, family or run changed (DECISIONS.md 9.173).
    • - src/analyse/run_view.html: MapLibre GL host replaces the Leaflet host - Esri Canvas / imagery / label rasters as sources; coast, water, green, sand, roads, rail and tram from basemap.json and the congested links from hotspot.json as GeoJSON sources with data-driven paint (delay colour, volume width and opacity, worst on top); metre-true road widths and per-class appearance zooms computed from the study latitude the basemap or the run supplies. A 3D switch: Terrarium raster-dem terrain (AWS Open Data) pre-fetched behind a flat hillshade from page open, OpenFreeMap building extrusions, sky and atmosphere; globe projection with the allowed tilt easing from 75 degrees at zoom 12 to 0 at zoom 5, set on the transform so animations are clamped, not stopped. Controls: ctrl / shift / command + drag turns and tilts linearly, the right button is inert, shift + arrows, ctrl+shift+N / U / F, no box zoom, a compass rose that levels the view. The land & water chip is plain-named and inert on satellite. The offline hand-drawn host is unchanged. First view: the basemap's coast extent, then the run's box; mppAt() falls back to the basemap's latitude, then the equator.
    • - docs/DECISIONS.md: section 9.173, its index row and its change-log row.
    • - Scratch Edge on arm 0 (20260912T202242_300it_25pct, 221,919 loaded links): a frame-gap probe through an ease to zoom 8.5, an ease to 14.5 with a pan, a 400 px pan and an ease to 11 - 430 frames, median 7 ms, worst 37 ms, none over 50 ms. 3D switch at zoom 14.2 on satellite: fully loaded in 1.7 s. Tilt clamp: 58 at z14, 43 at z9, 0 at z3. Shift-drag +50/-50 px: bearing +20, pitch +20, centre unchanged; right-drag: nothing; ctrl+shift+F: 0/0. Zero console errors in both themes and at 420 px; node --check on the script block.
    • - python src/run/session_gate.py --handoff: 22 of 22 gates and the three close-out checks pass; check_hardcoding.py --strict 0; document shape, links and currency 0.

    ## Summary The run viewer's congestion colour over-measured: the qsim's one-second step and a bus's stop dwell were counted as delay, painting 35 % of the routers pair's iteration-28 links "stopped". The telemetry and the viewer now measure road-traffic delay the way a map app states it, and the eight viewer defects the user reported were worked one at a time, each verified by measurement in a browser. The user took D4: a one-field control arm is read against arm 0 inside F35. No model value or target moved; no family opened; no arm launched; .tools/classes is not rebuilt under the running arm. ## Changes - src/java/citysim/RunTelemetry.java: transit vehicles leave the link accounting (a bus's dwell is not traffic delay); a 24-bin delay histogram per link for the day and the live window; the payload row is [id, volume, typical, mean] with typical = 1 + max(0, median delay − 1 s) / max(free-flow, free-flow of 150 m); the header states statistic, tolerance_s, min_stretch_m.     ## Summary The routers pair 20260915T000704_250it_25pct (C.raptor.mode_cost_representation = mode_constant, 250 iterations, 25 %) ran every iteration and shut down cleanly after 27.39 h, but its harness had died at iteration 34 (the launch was not detached, and the previous session's shell took it), so no _run.json was written and session_gate.py went red on the stale running record. The framework's only path for the state would have marked the result failed on a survivable Guice throwable. The user chose (D5) to add a sanctioned close-out; the run is the third RESULT, read against arm 0 inside F35, and it moves nothing outside one build's noise. ## Changes - run.py --close-out <run> / run_matsim.close_out_orphan: closes out a stale running card whose recorded pids are dead, whose log ends in MATSim's clean shutdown with no unexpected-shutdown request, and whose last ENDED iteration - read from the log by the new _iteration_times_from_log, never from the digest - equals the declared horizon; writes ran_to_last_iteration through the existing close_out(), the summary, the metrics and the processed mirror. A live run, a run short of its horizon, an unclean s
