    • The fifty-fourth session (16–17 September 2026, record section 9.177). Report #12 was lodged on the routers pair; the scoring pair (RUN.replanning.score_msa_representation = at_innovation_cutoff, the user's D7) was launched on a 25 % probe price and ran to its horizon in 25.77 h: it is the fourth result of F35 and moves nothing against arm 0 (car +0.007 pp, bike −0.292 pp, light rail 772 → 928 boardings, 2 of 12 inside and 6 past the bar on both), and the cutoff snap stands at car +1.76 pp under score averaging — the scoring branch is exonerated alongside the routers branch. The report's findings were worked without a run: the launcher detaches by default (D6), a run carries its own residents map (#213), the pricer no longer books a dead harness's iterations as setup, a finished orphan is closed out at the next launch, the issue gate reports a measurement that has come due, and three readers become one command each. A reading error in two earlier record sections is corrected on the position pages: MATSim's mode-choice coverage is a share of trips, not agents, so ride's coverage is the bound trips' share sitting at its target, and its deficit is what bound trips execute as (59 % ride; car-available escort members drive half of theirs). The user took D8–D12; the roots rebuild is re-scoped on that evidence and is the lane.
    • Nothing here is a finding about the city; no target value changed; the 67/143 holdout is untouched; no family opened.
    • Closes #213, #225, #227.
    • - Report #12 at docs/reports/20260916T062246_project_report.html (91 findings, 59 ledger rows, 20 recommendations) with the reference library refreshed; the ordinal re-keyed everywhere it is typed.
    • - Registry 558 → 567 fields (B.mode.seed_table, A.lightrail.dwell_sd_s, D.landuse.levels_by_building_type, CAL.targets.prepandemic_window, CAL.targets.current_window_start, RUN.machine.build_xmx, RUN.machine.gc_collector, RUN.gate.reader_timeout_s, RUN.storage.reader_timeout_s); the categorical check tests a declared value against its own sweep; CONFIG_REFERENCE and the schemas regenerated.
    • - Tests: test_run_residents_map.py, test_refactor_tools.py, test_harness_readers.py, additions to the close-out, issue-gate, concurrency and arm-cost tests; the import sweep compiles (never imports) the nine adapters that work at module level (#232).
    • - Documents: DECISIONS §9.177 with its index and change-log rows; nine position pages restated and stamped; the board; lane.json (the scoring pair done, the Java fold added, the roots rebuild unblocked); recommendations.json (nine of report #12's twenty taken); the brief rewritten from the template; GOAL.md's loop states the gate's scoped departure (D10); 31 archived banner links re-aimed and the link check extended; the data dictionary city-relative.
    • - python src/run/session_gate.py --handoff — every gate and the close-out checks PASS on the idle machine (toolchain compiled; unit suite 547 passed, 1 skipped).
    • - Each staged builder rebuilt its artefacts byte-identically (plans, chains, the 30 run-input sets, the targets, the corridor layers, the land-use parking layer) — recorded in the commits that staged them.
    • - The scoring pair read with python src/analyse/compare_runs.py 20260912T202242_300it_25pct 20260916T063903_250it_25pct --modes; its bound trips, wharf market and demographics with the three readers; all mirrored under results/processed/.
    • - A run made before this change and read after it without a _residents.csv.gz falls back to the city's current population with a WARNING; the three F35 results were backfilled.
    • By hand this session, and codified in the same tree: the bound-trips reading (measure_bound_trips.py), the near-wharf reading (measure_near_wharf.py), the residents backfill (extract_metrics.py --write-residents), the due-measurement scan (issue_gate.py), the stage extraction (split_stages.py, extract_loop_body.py). Still by hand: mirroring a reader's JSON into results/processed/ after the run has closed (results_store.mirror exists; the readers do not call it) — a one-line addition for the next session that touches a reader. Seven patch scripts for the roots rebuild and the Java fold were prepared in a session scratchpad and are attached to their issues (#86, #94, #107, #196, #215, #30) so they are not re-derived.

    summary_excerpt
    ## Summary Codex can load this project's conventions and workflows through native instructions and skills. Project-specific support stays under .agents/, while global skills and MCP credentials remain in user configuration. ## Changes - Adapt onboard, handoff and project-report, including report helpers and staged references, to native Codex questions, process sessions and delegation. - Add a configuration helper that preserves user settings and backups, plus source hashes and verification evidence for the inherited global skills and four MCP registrations. - Record the session in DECISIONS.md §9.178, update the monitoring position, regenerate the board and replace the next-agent brief. - Keep #210 open with the actual enforcement limits. Record the separately discovered package-audit defects in #234 and #235. ## Testing - Full onboarding and handoff gates, including unit tests and the idle-machine toolchain verification. - Document shape, currency, links and generated-board checks. - Six skill validations; effective native prompt confirms project instructions and project/global skills. - Configuration checks cover preservation, backup bytes, idempotence, multiline settings

did_fidelity_move_a_validation_figure
YES, the one stored case in this library: v6 replaced typed free speeds with free speeds calibrated by a SUMO microsimulation plus routing-API travel times, and reports car speeds by hour inside the routing-API bounds - a physical-fidelity substitution reported as a validation figure. Counts stayed 'generally too low, particularly on motorways'.
signals_addendum_2026_09_14
Ziemke & Braun 2021 (Procedia CS 184:745-752, doi 10.1016/j.procs.2021.03.093; VSP WP 20-40 read in full): OSM-derived signals and lanes were added to the Open Berlin Scenario and 'one iteration of the co-evolutionary algorithm was run to verify that the automated generation of signal and lane data results in a connected and correct network' - the 'verification' is structural, not against counts or travel times. Default fixed-time plans from German guidelines (90 s cycle, 10 s minimum green, 5 s all-red; extra green by lane count): 'This signal plans do not necessarily model a realistic signal control.' 'As the simulation of traffic signals and lanes in MATSim significantly increases runtime, the automated generation tool provides a possibility to ...' restrict the signalised area; 'only MATSim's Dijkstra implementation works with lanes, which is comparably slow.' Whether signals move a count fit in Berlin remains UNMEASURED in the published record.

    calibration_tooling
    Three named routes, all read this pass: (1) matsim.calibration in matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools - an ASCCalibrator driving an Optuna study, whose update is literally log(z_i) - log(m_i) - (log(z_0) - log(m_0)), i.e. the classic ASC fixed-point loop normalised on a fixed reference mode, with a pluggable learning-rate scheduler and a TerminationCondition dataclass whose check_termination carries "# TODO: not used yet"; (2) Cadyts, a Bayesian count calibration that adjusts NO parameter and instead adds a utility bonus so agents select the plans matching observed counts; (3) opdyts (Flotterod, TR-B 2017), which approximates point equilibria of the mobsim/scoring/replanning loop, with a Berlin mode-constant example. See calibration_methods. | 2026-09-14: the METHOD NOTE behind route (1) is now read in full - Rakow & Nagel, 'Automated calibration of alternative specific constants in agent based transport models', TU Berlin, June 2024, doi 10.14279/depositonce-20593, CC BY 4.0, three pages. Verbatim: 'Perform a simulation run until convergence and collect all relevant trips. Let z_i be the reference mode share for mode i and m_i the simulated mode share. One ASC always has to be fixed (usually to 0); otherwise, the solution is not unique ... asc_i + ln z_i - ln m_i - (ln z_0 - ln m_0) ... Perform more simulation runs while updating asc_i by delta_i for all modes i, except i = 0 after each run. This is done until simulated mode shares are sufficiently close to the reference mode shares.' Proof given for two alternatives under fixed utilities; discussion: 'The proof assumes that utilities remain constant during simulation runs, which is often not the case ... it is recommended to adjust the update step delta_i by a fraction. This fraction can be modified based on the difference between simulated and reference mode shares.' No run count, no scenario, no fit figure, no distance term in the note; the tooling's ASCDistCalibrator adds distance-group constants with the same update. The idea is credited to Gunnar Floetteroed. This is the exact expression in this project's asc_fixed_point.py, and it is cited as the calibration tool by the Rotterdam-The Hague row (Li et al. 2025).
    carried_to
    2026-09-16
    restart_mechanism
    NO checkpoint/resume exists in the platform. The developer answer (Marcel Rieser, matsim-code-examples issue #834, 12 Dec 2022, read via api.github.com this pass): 'The plans in "it200/200.plans.xml.gz" are the plans after replanning, but before mobsim, in iteration 200. So you can use those to resume at iteration 200 (it should generate the same events file like the first run), and then continue with iteration 201.' and 'If you use the plans file of iteration 200, start the new run also with iteration 200.' ... 'The first iteration of a run never does replanning.' So a resume is a plans-file restart AT the checkpoint iteration, and only where a plans dump exists (writePlansInterval); everything since the last dump is lost. Memory rule of thumb from the same repository's issue #189: 'typically... around 100KB per agent. That is 1 GB per 10k agents' (mrieser, 2019-08-20); a ~1M-agent, 250k-link scenario needed 60-90 GB actual (mrieser); JVM total is ~25% above the reported heap (josiekre).

Every factor row (101)

A1AResidential location (fixed from census)UNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Residential self-selection is a measured but minority share of the built-environment effect: disentangling it by housing type in one study put self-selection at 15.2%, 30.7%, 18.5% and 5.9% of the total impact on vehicle kilometres travelled for the four housing types examined, and the effect is modest for the elderly and large for younger adults. The built-environment side remains the Ewing-Cervero meta-analysis, with every 5D elasticity inelastic. A residence fixed from the census therefore carries most of the built-environment effect and mis-states only the self-selected minority.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S02642751210018522026-09-07
A2AWorkplace locationUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Workplace location is a calibrated long-term choice in every activity-based practice: ActivitySim and CT-RAMP run a shadow-priced work location choice and validate residence-to-work flows against the census commuting table and the mandatory trip-length frequency distribution. What the field does NOT publish is a flow TOLERANCE. The FHWA validation manual chapter 3 states there are no criteria guidelines for trip-distribution checks, and AToM - the leading open Australian activity- and agent-based model, and the source of several of this project's own behavioural coefficients - validates work travel only as a MODE SHARE of work trips, against a stated plus-or-minus one per cent error threshold on the 2016 Census Method of Travel to Work: driving 74.8% simulated against 73.4% VISTA and 75.2% census; public transport 21.5 / 21.4 / 19.3; walking 2.1 / 2.5 / 3.7; cycling 1.6 / 2.7 / 1.7. Destination distributions are shown only VISUALLY, at SA3 level, with no quantitative flow metric reported, and non-work trips are far looser (walking 15.4% simulated against 23.1% in VISTA). The transferable benchmark for a workplace-location build is therefore: work-trip mode share inside about one percentage point of the census table, plus a visual destination check - not an origin-destination pair tolerance, which no Australian activity-based model publishes.https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2112.120712026-09-08
A3AVehicle ownership per householdUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Household car ownership is one of the strongest single predictors of mode: an increase in car ownership raises the probability of commuting by car and depresses active and transit modes, with a reported elasticity of -2.643 for the substitution of active modes. Income, household size, distance to centre, accessibility to shops/services/employment and intersection density are the dominant explanatory variables.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S13619209240004402026-09-07
A4AVehicle type (EV, e-bike)UNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.The e-bike evidence is now meta-analysed: across experimental studies, access to an e-bike adds about 5 km of daily travel and raises e-bike mode share by about 26 percentage points, while car use falls by about 2.4 km a day (a 10% drop in car mode share); single controlled trials report car share falling 21%, and older meta-studies put e-bike-for-car substitution at 43% of trips and 63% of mileage. The effect is context-dependent: where cycling is already high the e-bike substitutes conventional cycling; where it is low it draws from car and public transport. (Figures are abstract-level; the full text was not retrievable this pass.)https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/01441647.2025.24745562026-09-07
A5ALicence holdingUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Licence holding among people under 35 has fallen across Australia, the UK, the US, Canada and much of Europe: TfNSW reports 65.4% of 16-20 year olds licensed in 2017, 8.3 points below 2001 and 8.1 below 2009, with the proportion licensed at age 30 also declining cohort on cohort. The travel-behaviour consequence named is a greater reliance on getting a lift, especially in wealthy suburbs and high-car-ownership families, and more public transport, walking and cycling in less wealthy areas.https://www.transport.nsw.gov.au/system/files/media/documents/2017/Why%20are%20young%20people%20driving%20less%20-%20Trends%20in%20licence-holding%20and%20travel%20behaviour_0.pdf2026-09-07
A6APublic-transport passes / concessionsUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.A smartcard natural experiment on Dutch fares separates pass holders from single-ticket users: passengers on a monthly or annual subscription have the highest travel frequency per origin-destination pair per week - almost twice that of single-ticket users - and the estimated fare elasticities split cleanly between the frequent-user products (pay-as-you-go, student and subscription) and the occasional ones (end-of-month and single tickets). A pass converts the fare from a per-trip price to a zero marginal cost, and the behavioural response is the frequency, not the mode.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0967070X2100055X2026-09-07
A7ABicycle ownershipUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Ownership is high and use is low, and the two are only weakly coupled: the National Cycling Participation Survey (2011-2019) finds more than half of Australian households own at least one bicycle while cycling is 1.4% of daily travel; Melbourne apartment households own 0.86 bicycles on average, off-street bicycle parking more than doubles the odds a household owns one, and the correlation between household bicycles and regional cycling use is 0.238. Ownership is male, younger, more educated and higher-income; renting, apartment living and foreign origin reduce it.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S09658564240026352026-09-07
B1BActivity generation and schedulingUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Daily travel budgets are strikingly stable: the Sydney Household Travel Survey reports an average 81 minutes travelling per person per day and 24-30 km per person per day across regions, with average travel time steady over the reporting series while mode composition moved (weekday train trips +3.1%, bus +2.4%, walk-only +2.7%, vehicle driver -0.8%, passenger -0.2%).https://www.transport.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/media/documents/2017/HTS%20Report%20Sydney%202012-13.pdf2026-09-07
B2BJoint household decisionsUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Joint and partially joint travel is a material share of household tours: partially joint tours - where one or more passengers is dropped off or picked up mid-tour - make up close to 14% of all tour types in metropolitan areas, and households with more than one student at the same school very commonly serve them on one car tour.https://caee.utexas.edu/prof/bhat/ABSTRACTS/Childrens_Activity_Travel_Patterns_31July09.pdf2026-09-07
B3BEscort of childrenUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Escorting is modelled in practice as a nested choice: school tours split into outbound and inbound half-tours, each with pure escort / ridesharing / no escort and up to three household chauffeurs. Significant determinants are the chauffeur's employment status, age and flexibility at work, the child's age, household characteristics and the relative distances between home, school and workplace; mothers working longer hours and further from home are less likely to chauffeur.https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11116-015-9634-x2026-09-07
B4BTelework / work-from-homeUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Telework reduces commuting and business trips, most clearly for full-time teleworkers, but the effect on TOTAL distance is mixed and design-dependent: rebound effects (extra non-work trips) and residential relocation to longer commutes offset part of the saving, and one-worker households increase total travel - particularly by car - while two-worker households show no significant increase.https://doi.org/10.3390/urbansci90601992026-09-07
B5BDay-type differences (weekday, Saturday, Sunday)UNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Weekend travel has a different shape, not just a different volume: the sharp early-morning and mid-afternoon weekday peaks are absent on the weekend day because so few trips are to and from work, and social-recreational and personal-business travel spread more evenly across the day become the dominant influence; weekend travel raises car-pooling for both youth and adults but has no measured effect on transit use, and destination land use shifts toward residential.https://nhts.ornl.gov/2009/pub/Weekday%20Travel%20FAQ.pdf2026-09-07
B6BMobility impairmentUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.People with a travel-limiting disability are 8-10% of the population and make fewer trips - about 18.6% fewer overall in the Utah household survey, with the disparity largest on transit (4.21 against 5.71 trips a day) and smallest for driving alone - and they choose differently: a measured shift toward car-pooling, a lower value of travel time, and a transit share that stays low despite a 50% fare concession because access, not price, is the barrier.https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.117482026-09-07
C1CAttraction by purpose (jobs, floorspace, enrolments)UNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.The practice is settled on size terms: each destination alternative's utility is a set of impedance terms plus one size function, where the size term is total or industry-specific employment for work, school enrolment for education, and for non-work purposes only the relevant categories - retail employment for shopping, restaurant employment for meals - with households or population for social purposes. Estimation results then show purpose-specific impedance coefficients (e.g. -0.01 business to -0.11 daily shopping per minute in one reported model) around a shared size term.https://tfresource.org/topics/Factors_Affecting_Destination_Choice.html2026-09-07
C2CDistance decayUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.The gravity/spatial-interaction relationship declines with distance, time and cost; the two competing deterrence forms are the power law and the negative exponential, with the negative exponential generally the preferred form in transport application, and the estimated deterrence parameter is sensitive to the spatial arrangement of the study area.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S09600779150015872026-09-07
C3CConstraints at both ends (capacity)UNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.A doubly constrained model preserves both the origin and destination totals from trip generation while a singly constrained one preserves origins only; doubly constrained is the appropriate form where the attraction totals are more reliable than the friction factors, and the standard case for work location, where predicted flows should equal both worker totals and job totals - in activity-based practice this is implemented as shadow pricing on the work and school location choices.https://tfresource.org/topics/Trip_distribution2026-09-07
C4CIntra-zonal tripsUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Short trips are systematically undercounted in travel surveys - the undercount concentrates on short walking, cycling and car trips for shopping and leisure, and every national survey from 1977 to 2022 has undercounted total walk trips by omitting short walks to stops and car parks. More than 80% of walk trips are under 2 km, and walking and cycling behave as substitutes below 2 km.https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/01441647.2024.23194152026-09-07
D1DDeparture-time profile by purposeUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Departure time is a genuine choice, not a fixed profile: Small (1982) tied departure-time choice to a workplace constraint in the utility function, and travellers were willing to shift one to two minutes toward the early side, or one-third to one minute toward the late side, to save one minute of travel time.https://www.caee.utexas.edu/prof/bhat/reports/utc_report_167500.pdf2026-09-07
D2DSchedule delay / activity duration preferencesUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.The schedule-delay cost function is asymmetric: the unit cost of arriving late exceeds the unit cost of arriving early, the disutility falls linearly to zero as arrival approaches the desired time, and Small hypothesises a FIXED penalty component on the late side - arriving late is always bad, however slightly.https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schedule_delay2026-09-07
E1EIn-vehicle time and value of time by purposeUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.The value of travel time savings is the single best-evidenced coefficient in the field, established by repeated international meta-analysis, and it scales with income: a meta-analysis of 268 income elasticities from 49 studies (1968-2019) puts the income elasticity of VTTS at 0.67 (OLS), 0.77 (WLS) and 0.80 (random effects), below the unity convention still used in appraisal.https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/198772/1/1-s2.0-S0967070X23000720-main.pdf2026-09-07

The European review by de Jong and Gunn (2001), as tabulated by Litman, gives car-kilometres with respect to fuel price -0.16 short term and -0.26 long term (commuting -0.12 / -0.23), and car-kilometres with respect to travel time -0.20 short term and -0.74 long term; Goodwin (1996) gives urban-road vehicle travel with respect to travel time -0.27 short run and -0.57 long run. Litman's synthesis states the scaling explicitly: a -0.1 short-run elasticity of vehicle travel with respect to fuel price reflects a -0.3 long-run elasticity, which reflects about -1.2 with respect to total vehicle costs, because most vehicle costs (depreciation, financing, insurance, registration, residential parking) are fixed and short-run effects are about a third of long-run ones. Brons, Nijkamp, Pels and Rietveld's meta-analysis of gasoline-demand price elasticities (158 estimates) finds the demand response driven mainly by fuel efficiency and car ownership and to a lesser degree by mileage per car, with a long-run estimate about -0.46 for total fuel demand. On what a driver actually prices, the classic Transportation paper 'Perceived and actual costs of operating cars' finds the modal split consistent with drivers perceiving petrol costs only, which is why mode-choice models price car by a marginal per-kilometre cost rather than by full cost of ownership.https://www.vtpi.org/elasticities.pdf2026-09-14
H12HHabit, inertia and satisficing: does the agent re-optimise every day, or stick until a threshold is crossed?UNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Habit is one of the two strongest predictors of the mode a person uses, and it is a MEASURED effect, not a residual. Three meta-analyses put the pooled correlation between a habit measure and the travel mode used at r+ = 0.50 (Gardner & Abraham 2008), r+ = 0.42 (Lanzini & Khan 2017, 58 primary studies) and r = 0.47 (Hoffmann et al. 2017), against an averaged pooled car-use-intention correlation of r+ = 0.83 in Lanzini & Khan; the review of reviews that collects them (Javaid, Creutzig & Bren d'Amour 2020) notes the differences between the meta-analyses exceed their confidence intervals. In discrete-choice terms inertia is the tendency to stick with the past choice even when another alternative becomes more appealing: Cherchi & Manca (2011, Transportation 38:679-695) test eight specifications on an RP/SP dataset with a mixed logit and find a significant, mode-specific inertia that weakens with learning across the SP experiments; Cantillo, Ortuzar & Williams (2007, Transportation Science) model it as a randomly distributed inertia THRESHOLD with serial correlation. The route-choice literature measures the same thing as an INDIFFERENCE BAND: travellers do not switch unless the saving exceeds a threshold (Mahmassani & Liu 1999), and Zhu & Levinson (2016, Transportation) estimate lognormal bands on 78 GPS subjects around the Minneapolis I-35W bridge replacement, which explains why the new bridge attracted less traffic than its time saving predicted. Satisficing (Simon 1957) is the general form - search stops at a satisfactory alternative - and boundedly rational user equilibrium (Di & Liu 2016 review) is the assignment that follows from it. The magnitudes the field reports are correlations and thresholds, not a utility constant; a simulator represents habit either as a state-dependent term (past mode in the utility), as a switching threshold, or - as MATSim does - as a selection rule over remembered plans.https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1748-9326/aba0322026-09-14
F6FTravel-time reliability and route switching: the reliability ratio and the indifference band in route choiceUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Reliability enters route choice as a second attribute beside mean time, and the field's summary statistic is the RELIABILITY RATIO - the value of a unit of standard deviation over the value of a unit of mean travel time. Carrion & Levinson (2012, TR-A 46(4):720-741) review and meta-analyse the estimates and attribute their spread to measurement (which dispersion measure, SP versus RP, self-reported versus GPS times). The same authors' Minneapolis before-and-after study of the I-35W bridge (39 subjects with complete data, 78 GPS observations) shows how far the ratio moves with measurement alone: 1.30 (mean/SD) and 1.60 (median/SD) on SELF-REPORTED times against 0.42 and 0.77 on GPS-MEASURED times, and 0.83 / 0.39 on the mean-to-90th-percentile measure - a ratio above 1 with perceived times and below 1 with measured ones. Route SWITCHING is boundedly rational: travellers keep their usual route until the saving exceeds an indifference band (Mahmassani & Liu 1999; Zhu & Levinson 2016 estimate lognormal bands on the same 78-subject GPS panel and use them to explain why the replaced bridge attracted less traffic than its time saving implied). For a simulator this means (a) a reliability term in route cost needs a measured day-to-day time variance per link, which a single-day equilibrium simulation does not produce, and (b) the switching rate of the route-choice strategy is itself a behavioural parameter.https://findingspress.org/article/8330-uncovering-the-influence-of-commuters-perception-on-the-reliability-ratio2026-09-14
B7BImmobility: the share of persons who make no trip on the survey dayUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Madre, Axhausen & Brog (Transportation 34, 2007) treat the immobile share - persons not leaving home on the reporting day - as both a central result and a prime quality indicator of a travel diary survey: for a standard one-day, weekday-only diary it should lie in the range 8-12 %, and a higher figure signals soft refusal (respondents claiming not to have left the house) rather than a behavioural fact. Later panel work (Transportation 2022, weekly routines of employees and retirees) shows immobile days cluster by person and weekday, so a one-day rate understates the share of people who are ever immobile and overstates the share of habitually immobile people.https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11116-006-9105-52026-09-16
E27EHeavy rail: station access mode - walk, feeder bus, park-and-ride, kiss-and-rideUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Station access is a mode choice of its own and its split moves with distance and supply. In Sydney, walking is the access mode for about half of home-to-train trips and almost 90 % of home-to-bus trips (Daniels & Mulley 2013, from the HTS); TfNSW's rail-user analysis puts walk access at 48 % and walk EGRESS at 84 %, because the car is not available at the far end. Meng, Taylor & Scrafton (ATRF 2017) observed three Adelaide Gawler-line interchanges in 2010: Mawson Lakes - feeder bus 46 %, park-and-ride 27 %, kiss-and-ride 17 %, walk+bike 10 %; Elizabeth - bus 44 %, walk 37 %, park-and-ride 11 %, kiss-and-ride 7 %; Gawler (one occasional bus) - walk 43 %, park-and-ride 36 %, kiss-and-ride 15 %, bus 3 %. Their stated-preference model finds walking distance, bus access, bus waiting time, car access and car-park availability all significant, with age, income and gender effects. Outer-suburban Sydney stations surveyed by Ku-ring-gai Council read car-driver access at 35 % (17-52 % by station). The rule is that park-and-ride grows with distance from the CBD and with free station parking, and that a walk-only access model under-states the catchment of an outer station by roughly the car-access share.https://australasiantransportresearchforum.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/ATRF2017_114.pdf2026-09-16
E28EWalk-access distance to public transport: the catchment distribution behind a search radiusUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.Daniels & Mulley (JTLU 6(2), 2013) measured 1,906 home-to-stop walks in the Sydney HTS: the mean walk to public transport is 573 m (median 518 m, upper quartile 824 m); to a train station 805 m (median 749, upper quartile 1,018 m, n = 667); to a bus stop 461 m (median 364, upper quartile 655, n = 1,084); school-bus walks 360 m. Mode of the public-transport trip is the dominant determinant - supply and stop spacing, not the walker - and the distributions are right-skewed with a tail past 1.5 km. Ewing & Cervero's meta-analysis gives a transit-demand elasticity of -0.29 to distance-to-stop (a 10 % longer walk costs about 3 % of ridership). Planning rules of thumb (400 m bus, 800 m rail; NSW's 90 %-of-households-within-400 m daytime standard) are straight-line and shorter than the observed walks.https://www.jtlu.org/index.php/jtlu/article/view/308/3382026-09-16
I16ITravel-time and speed validation: the acceptance bar for link speeds and route travel timesUNVERIFIED this passFull implementation re-read unfinished; literature reused with original date.The FHWA Traffic Analysis Toolbox Volume III (2004; Wisconsin DOT targets, Table 4) is the profession's acceptance table for a calibrated traffic model: hourly link flows within 15 % for 700-2,700 veh/h (within 100 veh/h below 700, within 400 above 2,700) in more than 85 % of cases; the sum of link flows within 5 %; GEH < 5 on individual links in more than 85 % of cases and GEH < 4 on the sum; ROUTE TRAVEL TIMES within 15 % (or one minute if higher) in more than 85 % of cases; link speeds and bottleneck queuing judged visually. The 2019 revision (TxDOT's summary) replaces the fixed bands with a two-sigma band (95 % of simulated points inside) plus two accuracy criteria applied to every metric used for calibration, and requires at least two metrics. verdict

Reports have prompted substantial repair, but taken is sometimes only partial and the current ledger misses at least one completed item (archived links). Since report #12, the scoring control consumed 25.77 hours without moving the 2/12 band count. The coverage premise of the repeated roots recommendation was corrected by PR #233. This report is authorised as preparation for Mumbai; it should concentrate on city portability, observation coverage and mode-preserving sample validation rather than re-issue stale Newcastle prescriptions. Replication-band measurement, travel-time validation, representative mode supply and city-independent inputs remain relevant repeats; no claim is made that another report itself improves fit.

Alignment with the goal

current_newcastle
Two of twelve modes inside 10% on the scoring result; calibration remains unmet. Six package-audit failures in PR #236 mean full package consistency is unverified despite green session checks.
mumbai_implication
Do not copy Newcastle targets, household structure, modal eligibility, CRS or sample fraction as Mumbai observations. PR #4 proves data validity is weaker than executable validity; PR #233 proves coverage wording can misdiagnose a model; both require real second-city evidence.

Recommendations, ranked

Ranked by what each would prevent or move × how cheap it is. A repeat tag marks one an earlier report already issued; the process audit counts them against this report too.

  1. Scale both seats and standing places. code opens a family
    The latest 25% run retains full standing capacity.
    change: src/run/sample_population.py · guard: XML encoding and boarding-capacity tests
  2. Require every city mode before declaring goal completion. code no model change
    Scorable subsets can currently pass alone.
    change: src/calibrate/fit.py and city mode contract · guard: Missing, unscorable and physically absent mode tests
  3. Acquire a Mumbai inventory with observation dates and units. data opens a family
    An observation from another city cannot calibrate Mumbai.
    change: cities/mumbai acquisition registry, provenance and manifest · guard: Coverage by mode, operator, geography, date and input requirement
  4. Prove mode-specific sample fidelity. model opens a family
    Household, standing passenger and fleet interactions respond differently to sampling.
    change: Sampling validation protocol and paired reference experiments · guard: Rare-mode counts, headways, denied boarding, waits, travel times and joint-trip retention
  5. Represent on-demand empty travel and served waits. model opens a family
    Fleet availability calculations alone do not simulate physical operations.
    change: TaxiFleetEngine and operator-specific fleet mechanisms · guard: Routed empty mileage and executed wait-time tests
  6. Make fares and fleet types city-declared. code opens a family
    Unknown transit modes silently receive bus fares and generic capacities.
    change: PtFareChargeHandler and build_matsim_run_inputs.py · guard: Multiple operators and train formations in a second-city fixture
  7. Resolve the separate package audit before a new arm. code no model change
    Six failures remain despite green quick gates.
    change: tests/check_package.py and run-input report coverage · guard: Full-package audit
  8. Finish the interrupted review scopes. process no model change
    The report contains explicit unread areas.
    change: Project-report scratch reviews and factor classifications · guard: Fresh code evidence for every published factor status
